title: The Brazilian Beauty Ingredient Encyclopedia: N to Z
seo_title: Brazilian Beauty Ingredients Encyclopedia N-Z — Full Reference
seo_description: Alphabetical encyclopedia of Brazilian beauty actives N to Z — niacinamide, pracaxi, panthenol, taninoplastia, etc. Sourced from major brand catalogues.
excerpt: The second half of our Brazilian beauty ingredient encyclopedia — letters N through Z. Sourced from Honma, Salvatore, and Brae catalogues.
author: Tomás Costa
content:
The companion encyclopedia covering Brazilian beauty actives from N through Z. For A-M, see the first volume.

N

Niacinamide (vitamin B3)

Increasingly used in Brazilian scalp formulations. Anti-inflammatory and supports follicular health. Showing up in newer scalp ampoule lines.

O

Oleic acid (omega 9)

Penetrating fatty acid, nourishes the cortex. The active reason avocado, baru, and olive oils work as deep-penetration oils. Used across Salvatore Radiant Color conditioner.

Olive oil

Squalene-rich emollient. Part of multiple Brazilian multi-oil complexes (Brae Revival, Salvatore Resistance, Honma HHC).

Omegas 3, 6, 7, 9

Essential fatty acid panel. Brazilian leave-ins (Salvatore Nutri Curl, Vitality Blond) deploy omega 6/7/9 specifically for fibre nutrition.

P

Panthenol

See D-Panthenol in volume A-M. Cross-referenced for navigation.

Polyphenols

Class of antioxidants including TANINO. Found in tea, wine, oak bark. The Brazilian beauty industry has invested heavily in polyphenol-driven chemistry — Salvatore's TANINOPLASTIA® is the flagship example.

Pracaxi oil

Amazon rainforest oil with the highest behenic acid content known in commercial cosmetics. Anti-frizz and deeply emollient. Used in Salvatore Resistance.

Proteins (wheat, almond, oat, fibroin)

Plant proteins that replace structural mass in damaged fibre. Brae Revival uses a wheat + almond + oat triple-protein blend. Each has a different molecular weight, filling different cortex defect sizes.

P-Life (biodegradable plastic)

Honma's biodegradable packaging technology. Plastic packaging that breaks down under environmental conditions over 1-2 years instead of 200+. Used across Honma's sustainability-positioned product lines.

Q

Quaternium-class conditioners

Cuticle-smoothing agents. Used universally in conditioning products. Brazilian formulations tend to favour milder quaterniums in salon-grade lines.

R

Radiant Prism

Salvatore's bioester complex from rice, sunflower, olive, palm, and jojoba. Seals cuticles around fresh colour pigment. Foundation of the Radiant Color line.

Resveratrol

Antioxidant polyphenol from grape skin. Appears in some Brazilian colour-protection formulations as supplementary to Radiant Prism.

Rice bran oil

Inositol and ceramide-3 delivery. Part of Salvatore Radiant Prism complex.

Rosehip oil

Linoleic acid + retinol-class natural vitamin A. Antioxidant. Used in Brae Essential Oil Blend.

S

Salt-bridge actives (cysteamine, etc.)

Used in some Brazilian smoothing alternatives to formaldehyde. Lower-toxicity bond-modification chemistry.

Seaweed extract (algas marinhas)

Three-dimensional matrix film-former. See Algas in part 1. Critical to Brae Revival's wash-out resistance.

Sebum-mimetic oils

Oils whose fatty acid profile resembles natural sebum (macadamia, jojoba). Provide deep sealing without overload.

Shea butter (karité)

See Karité in part 1. Cross-referenced.

Shorea butter

Underused alternative to shea. Higher stearic acid content = denser sealing. Found in Brae Revival butter blend.

Silicones (noble)

Higher-grade silicone blends with better wash-out profiles. Used across Salvatore Vitality Blond Leave-In and Brae Bond Angel mask.

Sunflower oil

Vitamin E delivery, light carrier. Used across multiple Brazilian multi-oil complexes and in Brae Essential Oil Blend.

T

TANINO

The cornerstone Brazilian active. Polyphenol from acácia-negra bark. Built into all Salvatore Tanino Therapy lines + Tanino Colors permanent line. See deep dive.

TANINOPLASTIA®

Salvatore's registered smoothing protocol. Built on TANINO. Formaldehyde-free Brazilian smoothing alternative.

TANINNteract

Salvatore's technology in Tanino Colors — TANINO complex specifically tuned for colour application. Conducts active dyes and conditioning agents into the fibre.

TEA ADVANCED

Salvatore's hydration technology in the Hydra Fusion line. Combines glycerin, D-Panthenol, hydrolyzed collagen, and chia extract.

Tea tree oil

Antimicrobial, used in some scalp lines. Less common in mainstream Brazilian professional brands than the broader herb blends.

Tocopherols (vitamin E)

Antioxidant chain-breakers. Present in nearly all Brazilian oil-based products via the sunflower/argan content.

TT Plex

Salvatore's bond-protection system for bleaching. Three-product range: Total Injection Repair, Sérum Reconstructor, Fibre Force. See deep dive.

U

UVB filters (Homosalato, etc.)

Sun protection actives. Used in Salvatore Vitality Blond Leave-In Sérum.

V

Vitamin A

Cellular regeneration, antioxidant. Used in Salvatore Radiant Color mask and ampoule formulations.

Vitamin B5

See D-Panthenol / Panthenol.

Vitamin B7

See Biotin in part 1.

Vitamin C

Antioxidant. Increasingly used in newer Brazilian scalp ampoule lines.

Vitamin E

See Tocopherols.

W

Wheat protein (hydrolyzed)

Part of Brae Revival triple-protein blend. Mid-molecular-weight protein for cortex restructuring.

X

Xanthan gum

Natural thickening agent. Standard rheology modifier in many Brazilian masks and conditioners.

Y

Ylang ylang

Aromatic active. Used in some Brazilian luxury-positioned lines for fragrance and mild antimicrobial action.

Z

Zinc PCA

Used in some Brazilian scalp and anti-dandruff formulations. Regulates sebum production.

Closing notes

Brazilian beauty's competitive edge isn't a single hero ingredient. It's the combination of:

  1. Access to Amazonian and Cerrado actives (pracaxi, murumuru, baru, barbatimão) European houses can't reliably source
  2. Decades of formulation experience around polyphenol chemistry (TANINO)
  3. Sophisticated multi-active blends (15-herb, 15-oil complexes) European brands typically simplify
  4. Sustained R&D investment in proprietary technologies (Ionic-Pure, TANINNteract, Radiant Prism, TT Plex)

This is the chemistry literacy that explains why a Brazilian Tanino Therapy treatment feels distinct from a European mass-market mask. It's actually different chemistry, applied with depth that European brands don't routinely match.

title: What's New in Brazilian Beauty 2026: 8 Trends Worth Knowing
seo_title: Brazilian Beauty 2026 Trends — 8 Things Worth Knowing
seo_description: The 8 most important trends in Brazilian beauty for 2026 — gel colour systems, ionic-pure pre-chemistry, scalp diagnostics, hyaluronic-led care, more.
excerpt: Eight trends that define the 2026 Brazilian beauty landscape — from gel-based colour systems to ionic-pure pre-chemistry to clinical scalp diagnostics.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
Brazilian beauty in 2026 looks meaningfully different from 2022. Some trends caught on globally (bond protection, scalp care). Others are unique to the Brazilian formulation ecosystem. Here are the eight that matter most.

1. Gel-based colour systems

Cream-base permanent colour has dominated for 40 years. Salvatore's Colore Gel — launched 2026 — replaces the cream with a translucent polymer gel that delivers colour via micelle nano-spheres and seals it with a bioadherent shield. Faster, cleaner, more vibrant.

Expect competitors to follow within 18 months.

2. Ionic-Pure pre-chemistry as standard service

The Salvatore Ionic-Pure system (in the Revitalize Chemical line) makes a pre-bleach metal-removal protocol a 15-minute add-on to any chemical service. Predicts: by end of 2026, this becomes the standard for premium European salons running blonde books.

3. Clinical scalp diagnostics as paid service

Trichoscope + Salvatore Pure Scalp protocols turn scalp care from "we sell shampoo" into "we diagnose and treat scalp conditions." Higher-margin, recurring revenue. European salons adopting this in 2026 typically see 25-40% revenue uplift per scalp client.

4. Hyaluronic-acid-led daily care

Brae Essential made hyaluronic acid mainstream in Brazilian hair care. The 13-SKU line uses HA as the hero across shampoo, conditioner, masks, ampoules, fluids, and oils. Expect other Brazilian brands to launch HA-led lines through 2026-2027.

5. Mix Therapy / custom protocol literacy

The era of "one mask treats all damage" is ending. Salvatore's Mix Therapy recipe book (20+ named custom protocols across the 7 sub-lines) sets the standard. Salons that name their services after specific protocols ("Resset Reconstruction," "Hair Transition," etc.) signal expertise — and charge accordingly.

6. Curl-literate formulation

Salvatore Nutri Curl & Waves' Day-After spray is the marker product — it signals that the formulators understand how curl wearers actually live with their hair (curl shape degrades after sleep, refresh between washes). Expect more curl-literate products through 2026, including refresh sprays and humidity-resistant finishers.

7. Bond protection as table-stakes

Five years ago, bond protection was a premium upsell. In 2026, every reputable Brazilian brand has its own system: Honma H-Bond Plex, Salvatore TT Plex, Brae Bond Angel. Bleach services without bond protection are increasingly seen as substandard practice.

8. Sustainability as commercial signal

Honma's P-Life biodegradable plastic. Salvatore's "eu reciclo" seal and cruelty-free positioning. Brae's clean line architecture. Sustainability isn't a niche position anymore — it's commercial signalling that the brand can compete in EU markets where these claims carry regulatory and consumer weight.

What doesn't show up in 2026 but might in 2027-2028

Microbiome-targeted hair care

Skin care discovered the microbiome 5 years ago. Hair care is starting. Expect the first "scalp microbiome" Brazilian products by 2027.

AI-personalised regimens

Brazilian brands have the data (Mix Therapy recipe variations × hair conditions). Expect AI consultation tools paired with diagnostic apps by 2027-2028.

Lyophilised actives

Freeze-dried active ingredients reconstituted at point of use. Standard in skincare premium tier. Coming to Brazilian hair care.

title: Brazilian Hair Care in London 2026: Where to Find It, How to Book
seo_title: Brazilian Hair Care London 2026 — Salons, Products, Where to Buy
seo_description: The 2026 guide to Brazilian hair care in London — salons offering Honma, Salvatore, Brae services. Where to buy retail. Distributors for trade.
excerpt: London has become one of the strongest European markets for Brazilian hair care. Here's the 2026 map — service-day salons, retail availability, trade distributors.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
London has become one of the strongest European markets for Brazilian hair care. The combination of a large Brazilian-Portuguese diaspora, humidity-driven demand for smoothing services, and increasingly chemistry-literate consumers has built a serious salon and retail ecosystem.

Here's the 2026 map — where to find services, where to buy retail, and which trade distributors carry which brands.

What's available in London (by category)

Brazilian smoothing

Most premium London salons running Brazilian smoothing offer either Honma Coffee Premium or Salvatore TANINOPLASTIA®. Both are reliably stocked through UK distributors.

Typical pricing in London (mid-2026):

  • Short hair: £180-240
  • Medium hair: £260-360
  • Long hair: £340-480
  • Plus retail home-care: £55-110

Colour services with Brazilian brands

Tanino Colors permanent and Salvatore Colore Gel are increasingly stocked in London colour salons. Mostly available through certified Salvatore Educacional graduate technicians.

Reconstruction and damage rescue

Brae Revival, Salvatore Resistance, and Honma H-S.O.S Capilar all available through specialised salons. The damage-rescue category is where chemistry literacy matters most — choose a salon with explicit Brazilian brand certification.

Scalp services

Still niche in London — only 5-10 salons currently run Salvatore Pure Scalp as a diagnostic service. Expected to grow significantly through 2026.

Curl care

Strong demand from London's Afro-Caribbean and Brazilian diaspora communities. Salvatore Nutri Curl & Waves available through specialised curl salons in West London and South London.

Where to buy retail (consumer-facing)

Brae

Direct retail via braehaircare.co.uk and through salon partners across the UK.

Honma Tokyo

Salon-only for most professional SKUs. Some retail availability through authorised resellers — verify CPNP registration before purchase.

Salvatore

Mostly salon channel. Limited direct retail availability for professional-tier lines.

Keratin and Care (multi-brand)

UK importer of Brazilian premium brands. Site: keratinandcare.com

For trade buyers (salons, distributors)

BM Supplier

UK and EU trade distributor for premium Brazilian brands. Stocks Brae, Salvatore, Honma, Cadiveu and others. Site: bmsupplier.co.uk

Direct importation

For larger volume (full container loads), direct importation from Brazil viable. Requires CPNP/SCPN registration handling. See our importing checklist.

Certification programmes in the UK

Salvatore Educacional

Periodic certification courses in London — TANINOPLASTIA®, Mix Therapy, scalp diagnostics. Announced via distributor network.

Honma Brazil

Annual UK certification sessions, typically Q2 and Q4.

Brae

UK certification through Brae's UK partner. Smaller scale than Salvatore Educacional but accessible.

Neighbourhoods to know

South London (Vauxhall, Brixton, Stockwell)

Strong Brazilian-Portuguese diaspora. Concentration of Brazilian-staffed salons offering authentic Brazilian smoothing services. Lower price tier than central London.

West London (Notting Hill, Bayswater, Kensington)

Premium tier. Salons offering full Salvatore Mix Therapy and Honma certified services. Higher price point, longer wait lists.

East London (Shoreditch, Hackney, Dalston)

Curl-focused community. Brazilian curl care lines (Nutri Curl & Waves) more concentrated here. Growing scalp service availability.

North London (Camden, Islington)

Mixed market. Higher availability of mid-tier Brazilian services with good retail attach.

Questions to ask any London salon offering Brazilian services

  1. Which Brazilian brand do you use? (Should name a specific brand, not "Brazilian keratin")
  2. Is the brand CPNP-registered for the UK? (Yes is the only acceptable answer)
  3. Is the technician certified by the brand? (Should be able to produce certificate)
  4. Do you do bond protection for bleached hair? (Should explain H-Bond Plex / TT Plex / Bond Angel)
  5. What's the home-care prescription? (Should be specific brand + frequency)

If the salon can't answer these clearly, look elsewhere.

title: Honma Coffee Premium: A 6-Month Real-World Test
seo_title: Honma Coffee Premium 6-Month Review — Real Results
seo_description: Six-month test of Honma Coffee Premium Keratin on three different hair types — virgin, coloured, bleached. Results, maintenance, what works.
excerpt: We tested Honma Coffee Premium for 6 months on three different hair types — virgin curly, coloured wavy, bleached blonde. Honest results.
author: Sofia Almeida
content:
We ran a 6-month real-world test of Honma Coffee Premium Keratin across three different hair types — virgin curly hair, colour-treated wavy hair, and bleached blonde hair. Each test ran with full home-care protocol. Here's what happened.

Test setup

Subject 1 — Virgin curly hair

3B curl pattern, no previous chemical services in 24 months, medium-coarse texture, mid-back length. Daily heat styling habit.

Subject 2 — Colour-treated wavy hair

2C wave pattern, brunette base with single-process colour every 8 weeks, medium texture, shoulder length. Occasional heat styling.

Subject 3 — Bleached blonde hair

Originally 4A, lightened to platinum 12 months prior, multiple bleach sessions, low porosity at roots, high porosity at lengths and ends, fine texture, mid-back length. Frequent heat styling.

Service execution

All three services followed the standard Honma Coffee Premium protocol:

  1. Two cleansing washes with Honma cleansing shampoo
  2. Apply Coffee Premium, work into each section, pause 35-40 min depending on hair resistance
  3. Rinse, towel-dry, blow-dry to 100% dry
  4. Flat iron at appropriate temperature for each subject's fibre profile

For Subject 3 (bleached): added H-Bond Plex to the Coffee Premium mixture for bond protection.

Initial results (week 1)

Subject 1 (virgin curly)

Most dramatic visual change. From 3B curl pattern to soft S-wave. Frizz eliminated. Fibre felt soft and pliable.

Subject 2 (coloured wavy)

Smooth, glossy, predictable result. Colour slightly toned darker (typical of any thermal service on coloured hair). No breakage.

Subject 3 (bleached blonde)

Result was good but porosity gradient produced uneven smoothing — roots remained slightly textured while lengths went very smooth. Mid-shaft section showed slight rigidity (early sign of over-processing on high-porosity sections).

Month 1 progress

Subject 1

Hair settled into a comfortable wave. Daily wash with Honma Bamboo CocoLux + H-S.O.S Repair mask 2x/week maintained the smooth finish.

Subject 2

No measurable change from week 1. Stable.

Subject 3

Mid-shaft rigidity persisted. Started weekly H-S.O.S Capilar treatment to address the affected section.

Month 3 progress

Subject 1

Result holding. Some curl pattern starting to return at the new growth at the roots (expected). Mid-lengths and ends still smooth.

Subject 2

First colour service post-smoothing (week 8). Colour took normally. Slight tone shift (cooler than usual). Smoothing held through the colour service without re-treatment needed.

Subject 3

Mid-shaft rigidity resolved with the H-S.O.S Capilar protocol. Overall result good but visibly more processed than Subject 1 or 2. Required more daily home-care.

Month 6 results (test conclusion)

Subject 1

Roots ~5cm of new growth showing natural curl. Mid-lengths still smooth. Hair pattern is now bi-textural — easy to manage, doesn't require constant heat styling. Verdict: highly successful.

Subject 2

Two colour services completed during the 6-month period. Smoothing held throughout. Subject reports significantly reduced daily styling time. Verdict: successful.

Subject 3

Result faded faster than Subjects 1 and 2 — by month 5 the smoothing was noticeably less pronounced. Some breakage at the most-porous sections (ends). Verdict: conditional success — works on bleached hair but requires more intensive home-care and shorter service intervals.

What we learned

1. Strand test matters

Subject 3's mid-shaft issue could have been predicted by a more thorough strand test pre-service. The porosity gradient on bleached hair requires section-by-section application timing, not one global pause time.

2. Home-care isn't optional

Subjects 1 and 2 maintained results because they followed the home-care protocol (Bamboo CocoLux daily, H-S.O.S Repair 2x/week). Subject 3 partially adhered — and showed faster fade.

3. H-Bond Plex is not optional on bleached hair

Subject 3's results would have been significantly worse without H-Bond Plex in the mixture. For bleached or chemically destroyed hair, H-Bond Plex isn't an upcharge — it's a safety requirement.

4. Service longevity varies by fibre type

Virgin curly: 5-6 months of meaningful effect. Coloured wavy: 4-5 months. Bleached: 3-4 months.

5. The chemistry is reliable

Across three very different hair types, Honma Coffee Premium delivered predictable, controllable results. No catastrophic failures (rigid fibre, chemical cuts, colour loss). For a salon service, predictability matters more than peak performance.

Would we use it again?

For virgin to colour-treated hair: yes, first choice. For bleached hair: yes with H-Bond Plex, but consider Salvatore TANINOPLASTIA® + TT Plex as the alternative for highly compromised fibre.

title: How to Read a Brazilian Hair Care Catalogue: A Distributor's Guide
seo_title: How to Read Brazilian Hair Care Catalogue — Distributor Guide
seo_description: How distributors and salons should read a Brazilian hair care catalogue — what to look for, red flags, marketing vs chemistry.
excerpt: Brazilian catalogues are dense documents. Here's how to read them like a distributor — what signals real innovation, what's marketing, what's missing.
author: Tomás Costa
content:
Brazilian hair care catalogues are dense documents. The good ones run 80-100 pages of products, technical sheets, application protocols, and brand history. Walking into a distributor meeting without knowing how to read them is like walking into a wine tasting without understanding labels.

Here's how distributors and serious salon buyers actually read these documents.

What the cover page tells you

Look for:

  • "Manual Técnico" or "Dossiê Técnico" — signals the brand treats their documentation seriously. Marketing brochures don't earn the "técnico" label.
  • Year of publication — older than 18 months = brand isn't innovating quickly.
  • Page count — 60+ pages typical for a serious professional brand. Less means either a new brand or a simpler portfolio.

Brand history pages

What matters:

  • Year founded + decades of operation (Honma early 2000s, Salvatore older, Brae newer)
  • Sustainability and certification seals — "eu reciclo," cruelty-free, ISO, etc.
  • Educational programmes mentioned — signals B2B commitment
  • International presence claimed — sets expectation for export readiness

Red flags

Brand history pages that are pure aspirational marketing copy without specific dates, certifications, or facility information. Real brands document specifics.

Hero technology pages

What to look for in a "hero ingredient" page:

  • Named active with a defined source (e.g., "TANINO from acácia-negra")
  • Mechanism of action explained, not just benefits listed
  • Cross-references to other parts of the catalogue where the active appears
  • Patents or registered names (the ® or "patenteado" mark) — signals proprietary chemistry

Red flags

Hero ingredient pages that name only generic actives (keratin, argan, coconut) without proprietary differentiation. That's commodity chemistry.

Line architecture pages

Image annotation: The diagram above shows Salvatore's seven sub-lines — Hydra Fusion, Nutri Curl & Waves, Pure Scalp, Radiant Color, Resistance, Revitalize Chemical, and Vitality Blond. This is the kind of architecture chart you'd assess when reading any Brazilian brand's catalogue.

Look for:

  • Clear distinction between lines (each solves a different problem)
  • Visual differentiation (colour-coding, distinct packaging)
  • Cross-line compatibility statements (Mix Therapy in Salvatore is the gold standard)
  • Clear positioning of professional-tier vs retail home-care

Red flags

Too many lines without clear distinction. If you can't explain in one sentence what makes line A different from line B, the architecture isn't real.

Per-product pages

The "5-element page" is the standard. A serious product page contains:

  1. Description — what the product is, for whom
  2. Key benefits — what changes for the user (3-5 bullet points)
  3. Frequency of use — daily, weekly, monthly
  4. How to use — step-by-step or precise dosage
  5. Active heroes — named ingredients with their role

What's missing from weak catalogues

  • No frequency of use specified
  • "Active heroes" listed as generic ingredients without role explanation
  • No pH mentioned (Salvatore lists pH for every product — gold standard)
  • No specific application instructions

Mix Therapy / recipe sections

This is the deepest signal of brand maturity. A brand that ships a recipe book of cross-line combinations is signalling:

  • Their professional channel is mature enough to mix lines
  • Their formulation team has tested cross-line compatibility
  • They expect their salons to think, not just follow line-by-line scripts

Salvatore's Mix Therapy is the most comprehensive recipe book in Brazilian hair care. Honma and Brae have less developed cross-line recipes — that's not a defect, just a different depth.

Technical infographics

Mechanism diagrams (how the chemistry works) signal R&D investment. The presence of mechanism infographics suggests the brand wants to be understood by chemistry-literate professionals — not just sold to.

Red flags

Catalogues with no mechanism infographics — only marketing imagery. Suggests the brand doesn't have proprietary chemistry to explain.

FAQ sections

A FAQ section at the end of a line (or the whole catalogue) signals that the brand has experience with the real questions distributors and salons ask. Brae includes detailed FAQ across line documents. Honma's catalogue includes targeted FAQs. Salvatore's dossier embeds FAQ-style content within technical pages.

Sustainability and compliance pages

Modern Brazilian brands document:

  • Sustainability initiatives (P-Life biodegradable for Honma, "eu reciclo" for Salvatore)
  • CPNP / international compliance
  • Cruelty-free positioning
  • Educational programmes

Brands without these pages aren't ready for EU/UK markets.

What you should NOT see in a serious catalogue

  • Before/after photos of unknown subjects — without methodology, they're marketing
  • "Miracle" or "transformative" claims without chemistry backing — regulatory red flag
  • Pricing in the catalogue — professional documentation doesn't price publicly
  • Discount codes or promotional offers — different document type entirely

Putting it together — the 30-minute catalogue review

  1. (2 min) Cover + year + page count
  2. (3 min) Brand history + certifications
  3. (5 min) Hero technology pages — note proprietary actives
  4. (5 min) Line architecture chart — count distinct lines, assess clarity
  5. (10 min) Sample 3-5 product pages — check 5-element structure
  6. (3 min) Mix Therapy / recipe section depth
  7. (2 min) Sustainability + compliance pages

That's enough to know if a brand is worth a follow-up meeting. The detailed line-by-line reading comes after.

title: The Salvatore Educacional Certification: What to Expect and Why It's Worth It
seo_title: Salvatore Educacional Certification Guide — TANINOPLASTIA® Training
seo_description: Inside the Salvatore Educacional certification — TANINOPLASTIA®, Mix Therapy, Ionic-Pure protocols. What courses cost, what they cover, ROI for salons.
excerpt: Why the Salvatore Educacional certification has become the most valuable Brazilian hair care credential a European technician can earn — what it covers, what it costs, what it returns.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
Salvatore Educacional has become the most rigorous Brazilian hair care training programme available to European technicians. Walk into any premium London or Lisbon salon offering Tanino Therapy services, and the master technician is almost certainly Salvatore-certified.

Here's what the certification covers, what it costs, and why it's worth it.

What Salvatore Educacional covers

The full certification is modular — typically 4-6 modules each lasting 2-3 days. Not every technician completes every module.

Module 1: TANINOPLASTIA® Foundation (2 days)

The base smoothing protocol. Covers:

  • TANINO active chemistry
  • Pre-service strand testing
  • Application techniques (A: Cuticle Prepper, B: Capillary Styling)
  • Iron temperature calibration
  • Home-care prescription
  • Common failure modes and rescue protocols

Required prerequisite for everything else.

Module 2: Mix Therapy Custom Protocols (3 days)

The recipe book. Covers:

  • 20+ named recipes across all 7 sub-lines
  • Dosage calibration for each recipe
  • Custom protocol design for specific client cases
  • Cross-line compatibility chemistry

Module 3: Ionic-Pure Pre-Chemistry (2 days)

The metal-removal system. Covers:

  • Metal contamination diagnosis
  • Pre-bleach protocol with Revitalize Chemical
  • Strand testing for metals
  • Failed-service rescue (greenish/orange bleach correction)

Module 4: TT Plex Blond Repair (2 days)

Bond protection. Covers:

  • Disulfide bond chemistry
  • Total Injection Repair dosage and mixing
  • Sérum Reconstructor application
  • Fibre Force post-service protocols
  • Compatibility with TANINOPLASTIA® and Colore Gel

Module 5: Tanino Colors + Colore Gel (3 days)

Colour services. Covers:

  • 60-tone Tanino Colors chart navigation
  • Colore Gel application (gel base vs cream base technique)
  • Ox Tanino developer selection
  • Special Mix and Super Clareadores
  • Tonalização (Creare semi-permanent)
  • Fast Effect bleach + Hairlights highlighting

Module 6: Pure Scalp Diagnostics (2 days)

Scalp services. Covers:

  • Trichoscope use
  • Scalp condition diagnosis framework
  • 15-herb blend protocols
  • Hair loss vs hair breakage differentiation
  • When to refer to dermatology

Where the courses run in Europe

Salvatore Educacional runs courses in:

  • UK — typically Manchester, London, Birmingham. 2-3 sessions per year.
  • Portugal — Lisbon. Higher frequency due to Brazilian-Portuguese language access.
  • Spain — Madrid, Barcelona. Growing programme.
  • Italy — Milan, occasional Rome. Established programme.
  • France — Paris. Smaller scale.

Courses run in either Portuguese (Brazilian) or English. Spanish for Iberian/Latin American audiences.

What the courses cost

Reference pricing in 2026 (UK/EU):

  • Module 1 (TANINOPLASTIA® Foundation): €450-650
  • Module 2 (Mix Therapy): €600-850

Plus product materials, travel, accommodation. Full curriculum cost typically €3,500-5,500 spread over 12-18 months.

What the certification returns

Certified Salvatore technicians charge 30-50% premium over non-certified. A "Master Technician — Salvatore Certified" position in the salon hierarchy commands the highest service prices.

Client retention

Salon retail attach

Service portfolio expansion

Certified salons can offer the full Mix Therapy menu — services that non-certified salons can't price-justify or deliver.

Common questions about certification

Do I need to be a qualified hairdresser to attend?

Typically 24 months before refresh recommended. New launches (Colore Gel in 2026) trigger update modules.

Can a salon owner attend without being a working stylist?

Some modules accept owner-managers (especially Mix Therapy + business modules). Service-execution modules require active stylist status.

Is the certification recognised outside Salvatore?

Within the Brazilian beauty industry, yes. Outside the industry, it's a Salvatore-specific credential. Combine with general professional qualifications (NVQ, HND, etc.) for full CV impact.

How do I find scheduled courses?

title: Brae's Line Architecture, Explained: Why Each Line Exists
seo_title: Brae Line Architecture — Essential, Divine, Revival, Bond Angel
seo_description: Why Brae structures their lines the way they do — Essential, Divine, Revival, Bond Angel, Soul Color, Defense. Strategic rationale + decision tree.
excerpt: Brae's six core lines aren't redundant — each solves a distinct problem. Here's the architectural rationale and how to know which line to recommend.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
Brae makes six core lines: Essential, Divine, Revival, Bond Angel (Blonde Repair), Soul Color, and Defense. To a new shopper, that looks like overlap. To a chemist or salon owner, each line has a distinct job.

Here's why each line exists and how to know which one belongs in your prescription.

The architectural principle

Brae structures their lines around fibre CONDITIONS, not generic categories. Each line targets a specific deficiency:

LineTargetsHero activeJob
EssentialDehydration + moderate damageHyaluronic acid + amino acidsDaily hydration + light repair
DivineFrizz + intense hydration needHydration intensive complexAnti-frizz + deep moisture
RevivalExtreme damage + porositySeaweed + triple proteinReconstruction for destroyed fibre
Bond AngelBleached + blonde fibreProtein blend + sheaBlonde reinforcement
Soul ColorColour-treated fibreColour-protective complexPigment retention
DefenseHair loss / thinningScalp ampoule activesFollicle support

Essential — the daily backbone

The widest line at 13 SKUs. Built on hyaluronic acid + amino acids + panthenol. Daily-use across all hair types with moderate problems (dryness, dullness, light frizz, mild damage).

Position: The "default" recommendation when you don't have a specific fibre problem to solve.

Two ampoules within Essential:

  • Intense Repair Ampoule — moderate damage
  • Anti-Breakage Ampoule — severe damage

The dual-ampoule design lets Essential handle the lower 80% of damage cases without forcing the client into Revival.

Divine — Essential's deeper sibling

Per Brae's own FAQ: "The Essential line promotes prolonged hydration and repair, while the Divine line promotes intense hydration and has anti-frizz action."

So Divine isn't a competitor to Essential — it's the deeper version when:

  • Hair is dehydrated beyond what Essential daily care delivers
  • Frizz is the dominant complaint (humid climates, curly hair)
  • Client wants weekly intensive treatment alongside Essential daily

Common stacking: Essential shampoo + conditioner daily, Divine mask once a week.

Revival — the rescue line

15 SKUs. For "chemically treated hair, with porous and extremely damaged strands." This is the line for clients who walked into the salon saying "everything is broken."

Hero actives: seaweed extract (three-dimensional matrix film-former), wheat + almond + oat triple protein, Shorea + shea butter blend.

Position: Salvage and reconstruction. Not for daily use unless damage is ongoing.

Critical difference from Essential Anti-Breakage Ampoule: Revival is a complete line (shampoo + conditioner + mask + ampoule + leave-in + sprays + oil). Essential Anti-Breakage is a single ampoule. Match the intensity to the damage severity.

Bond Angel — blonde-specific

For bleached, blonde, or highlighted hair. 7 SKUs (shampoo, conditioner, mask, leave-in across two sizes).

Different from Revival even though both target damaged fibre — Bond Angel is optimised for the specific damage profile of bleach (loss of structural protein, loss of natural lipids, ongoing oxidative stress). Revival is broader-spectrum.

Common combination: Bond Angel daily home-care + Essential or Divine mask 1x per week for the hydration layer + occasional Revival ampoule for active breakage events.

Soul Color — colour protection

For colour-treated fibre. Pigment retention focus. Brae's answer to colour fade.

From the Essential FAQ: "the Essential line is perfect for repairing strands damaged by the coloring process and for a better result it can be interspersed with the Soul Color line, which promotes colour protection."

Position: Specialty line for colour-active clients. Layered with Essential for daily hydration.

Defense — the scalp + anti-loss line

Different category entirely. Defense is a scalp ampoule applied to the scalp (not lengths), and NOT rinsed.

From the Essential FAQ: "The Essential Anti-Breakage ampoule offers the benefit of preventing hair breakage, while the Defense ampoule prevents hair loss. In addition, it is important to remember that the Defense ampoule, unlike the others, must be applied to the scalp and without rinsing."

Different problem (follicle vs fibre), different mechanism, different application.

The decision tree

Healthy fibre, daily care

→ Essential

Healthy fibre, frizz problem

→ Divine for mask, Essential for daily

Moderate damage, dehydration

→ Essential + Essential Repair Ampoule

Severe damage

→ Essential Anti-Breakage Ampoule for first intervention, escalate to Revival if persistent

Extreme damage, porous fibre

→ Revival (full line)

Bleached blonde

→ Bond Angel as base + Essential or Divine for hydration layer

Colour-treated

→ Soul Color for colour protection + Essential for hydration

Hair loss / scalp issue

→ Defense (scalp ampoule, no rinse)

What this architecture says about Brae

Brae's approach is "specialised lines, clean boundaries." Compare to Salvatore (7 sub-lines under one Tanino Therapy Exclusive umbrella) or Honma (5 lines distinguished by usage stage HSS/HHT/HHC/HCP/HPF).

Brae's architecture is the easiest to communicate to retail clients. Each line has a clear, declarative position. For salons running multiple Brae lines, the client communication is direct: "you need Bond Angel for the bleach AND Essential for the daily moisture." Easier sell than "you need Tanino Therapy Hydra Fusion + Vitality Blond + Resistance ampoule weekly."

title: The Layered Salon Model: Running Honma + Salvatore + Brae Together
seo_title: Layered Salon Model — Honma + Salvatore + Brae Strategy
seo_description: How premium salons run Honma + Salvatore + Brae as complementary lines instead of competing brands. Strategic stocking + service architecture.
excerpt: The premium salons in Europe don't pick one Brazilian brand. They run three — strategically layered. Here's how the model actually works.
author: Tomás Costa
content:
The strongest premium salons in Europe doing Brazilian hair care don't pick one brand. They run three — Honma + Salvatore + Brae — as a layered portfolio. Each brand occupies a distinct service category, with minimal overlap.

Here's how that model actually works, with stocking recommendations and service architecture.

The strategic logic

Brazilian brands aren't interchangeable. Each one has built distinctive depth:

  • Honma — heritage smoothing + accessible retail attach
  • Salvatore — deepest technical platform + premium services
  • Brae — cleanest line architecture + strong daily home-care

Running all three lets a salon offer the right brand for each service moment — without competing your own services against themselves.

The service layer architecture

Service categoryPrimary brandSupport brandRetail attach
Smoothing (entry tier)Honma Coffee Premium—Honma Bamboo CocoLux
Smoothing (premium tier)Salvatore TANINOPLASTIA®TT Plex if neededSalvatore Hydra Fusion home-care
Bleach (low-risk)(own choice) + H-Bond Plex—Honma HHC range
Bleach (high-risk)Salvatore Revitalize Chemical pre + TT PlexBrae Bond Angel postBrae Bond Angel + Salvatore Vitality Blond
Colour servicesSalvatore Tanino Colors or Colore GelHonma H-One postSalvatore Radiant Color home-care
Reconstruction serviceBrae Revival (full protocol)Salvatore Resistance ampouleBrae Revival home-care
Scalp diagnosisSalvatore Pure Scalp—Salvatore Pure Scalp home-care
Curl careSalvatore Nutri Curl & WavesBrae DivineSalvatore Nutri Curl home-care
Daily retail (general)Brae Essential—Same brand
Hair loss supportBrae Defense (scalp ampoule)Salvatore Pure ScalpBrae Defense

Why this isn't redundant

Salvatore handles depth (technical chemistry, custom protocols, scalp diagnostics, deep blonde support). Honma handles heritage smoothing services that clients book by brand recognition. Brae handles daily retail home-care across the broadest range of fibre conditions.

What would be redundant

Running Honma Coffee Premium AND Salvatore TANINOPLASTIA® as competing smoothing services. You'd cannibalise yourself. Instead, use one as the entry-tier service (Honma at £200-260) and one as the premium tier (Salvatore at £350-480). Different price points, different client targets.

Stocking budget allocation

Initial portfolio investment (€8,000-12,000 typical for new portfolio)

Honma allocation: 35-45%

  • Coffee Premium Keratin service stock
  • H-Bond Plex for bleach reinforcement
  • HHC Bamboo CocoLux retail line (full sizes)
  • HHT H-S.O.S Capilar for damage services
  • HPF retail finishing range

Salvatore allocation: 35-45%

  • TANINOPLASTIA® Products A + B
  • TT Plex Blond Repair System (3 SKUs)
  • Mix Therapy product set: Hydra Fusion, Nutri Curl, Resistance, Vitality Blond, Revitalize Chemical, Radiant Color masks (back bar)
  • Pure Scalp line (4 SKUs)
  • Selected home-care retail SKUs

Brae allocation: 15-25%

  • Essential retail line (shampoo + conditioner + mask + ampoules + finishers)
  • Bond Angel for bleach client retail
  • Revival line for damage rescue retail
  • Defense for hair-loss support

The service menu structure

Tier 1: Express (£60-120)

Single-product treatments. Essential mask + leave-in, Revival ampoule service, Coffee Premium glaze.

Tier 2: Standard service (£180-280)

Single-brand full protocols. Honma Coffee Premium Smoothing, Brae Revival 60-min Reconstruction, Salvatore Hydra Fusion Hydration.

Tier 3: Custom protocols (£280-450)

Salvatore Mix Therapy recipes. "Resset Reconstruction" + "Hair Transition" + "Soft Platinum" — named services with bespoke positioning.

Tier 4: Premium tier (£450+)

TANINOPLASTIA® + TT Plex + Revitalize Chemical pre-treatment + full Mix Therapy home prescription. The most-comprehensive service.

Retail attach strategy

Brae Essential as the universal retail attach across services. Brae Bond Angel for any bleach client. Salvatore home-care for clients who specifically book Salvatore services. Honma home-care for Honma smoothing clients.

This avoids the common error of trying to upsell every client into the same retail line. Each client gets the home-care that matches the service they received.

What technicians need to know

Multi-brand salons need technicians with cross-brand certification. Realistically:

  • 1-2 technicians Honma-certified (for Coffee Premium services)
  • 2-3 technicians Salvatore-certified (for TANINOPLASTIA® + Mix Therapy + Pure Scalp)
  • All technicians familiar with Brae Essential (the daily retail product line)

Cross-training is realistic over 12-18 months for a mid-sized salon.

Risks of the layered model

Inventory complexity

Three brands × full lines = 60-90 SKUs in stock. Stock management requires proper POS/inventory system.

Service-menu cognitive load

Clients can be overwhelmed by choice. Counter with clear menu tiering (above) and trained consultation upfront.

Training cost

Multi-brand certifications add up. Budget €5,000-9,000 per master technician for full cross-brand training.

Distributor relationships

Running three brands means three distributor relationships. Possible to consolidate through multi-brand distributors (like BM Supplier for UK/EU).

The salons doing this well

The pattern holds across our research: salons running €1.5M+ annual revenue with strong Brazilian hair care positioning typically run all three brands. They name their services after specific protocols (Mix Therapy recipes), price by tier, and train technicians cross-brand.

The pattern doesn't fit small salons (under €400k revenue) — the inventory and training overhead is too high. Stick to one brand and grow before adding layers.

title: How to Run a Honma HSS Coffee Premium Service — Salon Protocol
seo_title: Honma HSS Coffee Premium Salon Protocol — Full Step-by-Step
seo_description: Complete salon protocol for running a Honma Coffee Premium Keratin service. Pre-assessment, application, finishing, retail attach.
excerpt: The complete in-salon protocol for Honma's Coffee Premium Keratin — from porosity test to home-care prescription. For certified technicians.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
Honma Coffee Premium Keratin is one of the most reliable Brazilian smoothing systems available to European salons. The chemistry is forgiving but the service still has multiple failure modes — pre-assessment skipped, application uneven, finishing temperature wrong, home-care prescription weak.

Here's the complete protocol, end-to-end, for a certified technician.

Pre-service: client consultation (15 min)

1. Hair history audit

  • Last chemical service: type, brand, date
  • Bleach history: ever, when, how many sessions
  • Heat styling frequency
  • Pool/well water exposure
  • Any breakage in last 3 months

2. Visual + tactile assessment

Inspect roots vs mid-lengths vs ends. Note porosity gradient. Pull a clean strand and test elasticity — if it snaps under light tension, treat as porosity:high.

3. Strand test (mandatory)

Cut a discreet test strand. Apply Coffee Premium per the standard protocol on the strand only. Process. Iron-finish. Inspect: smoothness achieved? Fibre rigidity? Colour shift?

Stop signs: any strand discoloration, rigid feel, or breakage during the iron test = postpone the service. Run Honma H-S.O.S Capilar protocol 2x at 1-week intervals first, then retest.

Stage 1: Hair preparation (30 min)

  1. Two cleansing washes with Honma cleansing shampoo (high-clean, removes residue and product buildup). No conditioner.
  2. Towel-dry to 70-80% dryness.
  3. Detangle with a wide-tooth comb. Note any sections of unusual friction — these are highest-porosity areas, will need lighter Coffee Premium application.
  4. Section the hair into 4 quadrants with horizontal partings.

Stage 2: Coffee Premium application (45 min)

  1. Pour Coffee Premium into a clean bowl. Apply with a tint brush, working from the back quadrants forward.
  2. Application thickness: thicker on resistant areas (mid-lengths of virgin hair), thinner on porous areas (bleached sections, ends).
  3. Saturation: brush each section until the fibre is fully coated. Visible drip = too much. Dry patches = too little.
  4. Cover with a plastic cap. Process: 30-40 minutes depending on resistance.

Why timing matters

Under-processed: smoothing doesn't take, client returns in 6 weeks unsatisfied. Over-processed: cumulative cortex stress, especially on porous sections.

Stage 3: Rinse and dry (15 min)

  1. Rinse with lukewarm water until completely clear. NO shampoo at this stage.
  2. Towel-dry thoroughly.
  3. Blow-dry on medium heat, straight, smooth airflow. Hair should be 100% dry before iron stage.

Stage 4: Flat iron finishing (45-60 min)

  1. Iron temperature: 200-220°C on resistant hair; 180-200°C on coloured/porous hair.
  2. Section into 1cm slices. Iron each section 8-12 passes for resistant hair, 5-8 for porous.
  3. Watch for steam — light visible steam is normal, heavy steam means moisture still present (re-dry).
  4. The "smoke test": if visible smoke comes off the iron during the pass, temperature is too high. Drop 10°C.

Stage 5: Optional second rinse + sealing (15 min)

Some Coffee Premium protocols call for a finishing rinse 24-48 hours later. For most clients, the iron-and-go finish works. For clients with significant porosity, schedule a return visit at 48h for the finishing rinse and Honma HHC home-care prescription.

Home-care prescription (the retail attach)

Day 0-3 post-service:

  • No washing (let chemistry stabilise)
  • No hair ties, no clips, no pinning back
  • Sleep on silk pillow

Day 4 onwards:

  • Daily: Honma Bamboo CocoLux Fusion shampoo + conditioner
  • 2x per week: Honma H-S.O.S Repair mask for moisture retention
  • Pre-styling: HPF thermal protection

Pricing the service

Reference range for Coffee Premium in European salons (mid-2026):

  • Short hair (above shoulders): €180-220
  • Medium hair (shoulders to mid-back): €240-300
  • Long hair (below mid-back): €300-380
  • Plus retail home care: €60-120 attach typical

Add 15-25% premium for: Bond protection on bleached sections (H-Bond Plex), priority booking, master-technician service.

Common failure modes

  1. Streaking after first wash — Coffee Premium was uneven during application. Re-apply lighter pass after 4 weeks.
  2. Fibre rigidity / dryness — Iron temperature too high, or over-processed. Run Honma H-S.O.S Capilar weekly for 4 weeks.
  3. Result fading at 6-8 weeks — Home-care didn't happen, OR client washed too soon. Re-educate on home-care protocol.
  4. Greenish tint on bleached sections — Metals in the bleach reacting with the Coffee Premium. NEXT TIME: pre-treat with Salvatore Revitalize Chemical or equivalent metal detox before applying Coffee Premium.

title: The Pre-Bleach Protocol Every Salon Should Run with Revitalize Chemical
seo_title: Pre-Bleach Protocol — Revitalize Chemical Ionic-Pure
seo_description: Step-by-step pre-bleach protocol using Salvatore Revitalize Chemical to remove metals before lifting. Prevents green tints, breakage, colour failure.
excerpt: The 15-minute pre-bleach intervention that prevents the bleach failures nobody can explain. Step-by-step protocol for the Ionic-Pure system.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
You bleach a client. The result is greenish in some sections, orange in others. The fibre feels rigid in places. She swears she's done nothing different. The bleach formula is your standard one.

The villain isn't the bleach. It's the metals already in her hair — copper from old plumbing, iron from well water, calcium from hard water. These react violently with hydrogen peroxide. The 15-minute fix is the pre-bleach protocol with Salvatore Revitalize Chemical.

Who needs the protocol

Anyone you're about to bleach. But especially:

  • Clients with well water (rural, coastal)
  • Clients with old plumbing (most of Europe — pre-1970s housing)
  • Regular pool swimmers (chlorine + copper sulfate)
  • Anyone whose previous bleach showed unexpected tones
  • Any client requesting platinum lift (the highest-risk service)

The 3-step protocol (15 min before bleach)

Step 1: Wash with Revitalize Chemical shampoo

Apply to wet hair, work to lather, focus on length and ends. Pause 2 minutes. Rinse thoroughly with warm water.

Step 2: Apply Revitalize Chemical mask

On damp hair, apply the mask from mid-lengths to ends. Cover the entire fibre. Pause 10 minutes. Rinse thoroughly.

Step 3: Dry completely

Towel-dry, then blow-dry to 100% dry. The fibre must be dry before bleach application.

What's actually happening

The Ionic-Pure technology in both shampoo and mask works through chelation:

  1. Identification — The active is polarised to detect positive-charged metal ions in the cortex.
  2. Capture — Molecules wrap around the metal (chelation), neutralising reactivity.
  3. Expulsion — Chelated metal complexes lose adhesion to keratin and rinse out.

Why this matters more than you think

Safety angle — exothermic reactions

Metal + hydrogen peroxide can react violently. The salons reporting "chemical cuts" where bleach foils literally cut the hair often had metal-loaded clients. The 15-minute Ionic-Pure step prevents this.

Result angle — colour predictability

Copper turns lifted hair green. Iron produces orange undertones. Calcium blocks dye uptake. After Ionic-Pure, the bleach reaction follows the formula — no more "I don't know why it went green."

Fibre integrity angle

Metals cross-link with keratin in unnatural patterns, making fibre rigid and brittle. Removing them BEFORE the bleach preserves elasticity through the chemical service.

Pricing the protocol

Most salons add €15-25 to the bleach service for the pre-treatment. Position it as "pre-bleach detox" or "Ionic-Pure preparation." Clients who've had bad bleach experiences will pay the upcharge.

Common questions

"Can I just use a clarifying shampoo?"

No. Clarifying shampoos remove surface buildup (sebum, silicone, product residue). Ionic-Pure removes metals bonded inside the cortex. Different problem, different chemistry.

"Does the client need to come in early for this?"

Add 15 minutes to the appointment. Wash + mask pause + rinse + dry = 15 min realistic.

"Can I do this on bleached hair after the fact?"

Yes — after a failed bleach with greenish tint, run Revitalize Chemical, then re-tone. Often corrects the failure without another full lift.

"What about the home-care version?"

For clients with chronic metal exposure (well water, regular swimmers), the Revitalize Chemical Home Care kit is daily shampoo + conditioner, weekly mask. Protects between bleach services.

title: The Scalp Diagnosis Service: How to Add a New Revenue Stream with Pure Scalp
seo_title: Scalp Diagnosis Service Guide — Salvatore Pure Scalp
seo_description: How to build a scalp diagnosis service in your salon using Salvatore Pure Scalp. Diagnostic protocol, retail attach, pricing, certification path.
excerpt: Scalp care is the next premium category. Here's how to build a diagnostic service around Salvatore Pure Scalp — protocol, pricing, retail.
author: Dr. Rachel Okonkwo, MSc Trichology
content:
European salons are catching on to what dermatology and Asia have known for a decade: scalp care is the next premium category. Healthy hair grows from a healthy scalp. The salons offering scalp diagnosis as a service are seeing 25-40% revenue uplift per client.

Salvatore Pure Scalp is one of the few professional cosmetic-tier lines built for this category. Here's how to build the service around it.

What Pure Scalp is

A 4-SKU clinical scalp line: shampoo, mask, conditioner, and home-care kit. Built on a 15-herb blend with rosemary and menthol as the hero actives.

The 15-herb blend

Rosemary, aloe vera, arnica, rue, chamomile, horse chestnut, centella asiatica, comfrey, mallow, seaweed, burdock, bamboo shoot, witch hazel, mint, and barbatimão.

Each plant on that list has documented activity on microcirculation, sebum regulation, follicular stimulation, or anti-inflammatory response. Barbatimão in particular — a Brazilian Cerrado plant — is difficult to source outside Brazil.

The diagnostic service — 45 min

Stage 1: Consultation (10 min)

  • Hair loss pattern, if any (diffuse vs patterned)
  • Itching frequency
  • Dandruff or flaking
  • Sebum production (when does hair feel greasy?)
  • Hair density change over last 2 years
  • Recent medication or hormonal changes
  • Diet, stress, sleep baseline

Stage 2: Visual examination (10 min)

Examine the scalp under good lighting, ideally with a trichoscope (€200-500 entry-level devices available). Look for:

  • Inflammation patterns (redness, sensitivity)
  • Sebum distribution (where is it heaviest?)
  • Hair density across the crown
  • Follicular density
  • Visible flaking — distinguish dandruff (yellow, oily) from dry skin (white, dry)

Stage 3: Treatment (20 min)

Apply Pure Scalp shampoo — massage 5 minutes into the scalp. Pause 5 minutes. Rinse. Apply Pure Scalp mask — focused on scalp, not lengths. Pause 10 minutes. Rinse. Apply Pure Scalp conditioner to length only. Rinse.

Stage 4: Diagnosis + prescription (5 min)

Document findings. Recommend home-care:

  • Oily scalp + dandruff: Pure Scalp shampoo daily, mask 1x/week
  • Hair loss + healthy scalp: Defense ampoule (Brae) or scalp ampoule applied to scalp 3x/week (consult also dermatology for confirmed alopecia)
  • Sensitive scalp + irritation: Pure Scalp shampoo 2-3x/week, alternate with neutral shampoo
  • Dry scalp + flaking: Pure Scalp conditioner-focused, mask 2x/week, oil treatment 1x/week

Pricing the service

Reference range for European salons:

  • Diagnostic consultation + treatment: €60-90
  • Plus home-care kit attach: €45-65
  • Follow-up at 4 weeks: €40-60
  • Total first-cycle revenue per client: €145-215

Subscription model

Monthly maintenance package: €75/month (one in-salon treatment + Pure Scalp shampoo refill). This is the recurring revenue layer that builds.

Who pays for scalp services

Hair loss anxiety

Clients noticing thinning (post-pandemic, hormonal, stress-induced). Highest urgency, highest spend.

Recurring dandruff/seborrhea

Clients tired of over-the-counter products. Medium urgency, recurring revenue.

Pre-event (wedding, photography)

Need clean, healthy-looking scalp for visible parting. Low urgency, premium one-off.

Post-chemical-service recovery

Clients with scalp sensitivity after bleach or colour. High urgency.

Boundary: when to refer to dermatology

Pure Scalp is a cosmetic-tier intervention. NOT for:

  • Diagnosed alopecia areata (refer to dermatology)
  • Severe seborrheic dermatitis (refer to GP/dermatology)
  • Suspected scarring alopecia (refer immediately)
  • Any unexplained patchy hair loss

For these, position your service as supportive home-care alongside medical treatment, not replacement.

Certification and training

Salvatore Educacional runs scalp diagnostic certification courses. A 2-day intensive covers trichoscope use, the diagnostic framework above, and the Pure Scalp protocols. Highly recommended before launching the service commercially.

title: 40 Questions About Honma Tokyo, Answered
seo_title: Honma Tokyo FAQ — 40 Questions Answered
seo_description: Forty questions about Honma Tokyo — lines, products, application, salon use, importing, certifications — all answered from the 2024 catalogue.
excerpt: The forty most-asked questions about Honma Tokyo — from technical chemistry to importing strategy — answered with the brand's own documentation.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
Forty of the most-asked questions about Honma Tokyo, answered from the brand's 2024 catalogue and our own salon-side experience working with the line.

About the brand

1. Is Honma Tokyo Japanese or Brazilian?

Brazilian, but founded with strong Japanese-Brazilian heritage. Manufactured in Brazil, distributed worldwide.

2. How long has Honma been in business?

Founded in the early 2000s. By 2024, distribution across 40+ countries.

3. Is Honma CPNP-registered in the EU?

Most professional lines are. Check the specific SKU label or ask your distributor before importing.

4. Is Honma cruelty-free?

The brand documents cruelty-free positioning and sustainability commitments including the P-Life biodegradable packaging line.

About the five product lines

5. What are the five Honma product lines?

HSS (Hair Straightening System), HHT (Hair Treatment), HHC (Hair Care), HCP (Color Pro), HPF (Pro Finish). Plus Hair Tools as a separate category.

6. What's the difference between HHT and HHC?

HHT is professional in-salon treatment line (H-S.O.S Capilar, H-Bond Plex). HHC is home-care retail line (Bamboo CocoLux, H-S.O.S Repair).

7. Is HHC also professional-tier?

It's salon-grade but designed for home application. Same active classes, smaller volumes, simpler application.

Coffee Premium Keratin

8. Is Coffee Premium formaldehyde-free?

Yes, formaldehyde-free.

9. How long does Coffee Premium last?

3-4 months for most clients with proper home-care. Up to 5 months in low-humidity climates.

10. Can I do Coffee Premium on bleached hair?

Yes, with H-Bond Plex mixed in for bond protection. Without it, expect breakage at the bleached sections.

11. What's the iron temperature for Coffee Premium?

200-220°C for resistant hair, 180-200°C for coloured or porous hair. Drop 10°C if visible smoke from the iron.

12. How long is the Coffee Premium service?

2.5-3.5 hours start to finish, depending on hair length and density.

13. Can the client wash on day 1?

No. 72-hour rest period before first wash. Also no hair ties, clips, or pinning back during this period.

H-Bond Plex

14. What does H-Bond Plex do?

Protects disulfide bonds during bleach. Mixed into the bleach formula, not applied separately.

15. How much H-Bond Plex per bleach application?

Follow brand-specific ratio — typically 1:10 plex to bleach formula. Check current product instructions.

16. Can H-Bond Plex be used outside bleach (in colour, in smoothing)?

Yes — compatible with colour and smoothing chemistries. Reinforces fibre during any high-stress chemical service.

17. Is H-Bond Plex equivalent to Olaplex?

Similar category, different specific chemistry. Both protect bonds during chemical service.

H-S.O.S Capilar

18. What's the H-S.O.S Capilar protocol?

5-step in-salon rescue treatment for severely damaged fibre. See our dedicated guide.

19. How often can I do H-S.O.S Capilar?

Once per week for damaged hair. After 4-6 weeks, transition to home-care with H-S.O.S Repair.

20. Can I do H-S.O.S Capilar before bleaching?

Run it 2x at 1-week intervals before a high-risk bleach service. Strengthens fibre before the chemical stress.

HCP Color Pro & H-One Neutralizing

21. What does H-One Neutralizing do?

Resets fibre pH after colour services. Closes cuticles around fresh pigment.

22. How long after colour do I apply H-One?

Immediately after the colour rinse, before the standard conditioner.

23. Does the HCP toning range work on dark bases?

Yes, designed for darker bases. Standard toning protocols apply.

Hair Tools

24. What's special about the Honma flat iron?

Designed with the Coffee Premium and other HSS chemistries in mind. Temperature controls calibrated for Brazilian smoothing protocols.

25. Is the H-Brush worth the price?

For salons, yes. For retail clients with thick/curly hair, the H-Brush is one of the better professional-tier devices on the market.

Pricing & business

26. What's the wholesale margin for Honma in Europe?

Varies by distributor. Typical professional margin 40-55% on cost. Discuss with your distributor.

27. Minimum order quantity for Honma?

Distributor-specific. EU/UK distributors typically have moderate MOQs for new accounts.

28. What's the markup recommendation for retail home-care?

2-2.5x cost is standard. Bamboo CocoLux at €18-25 retail, H-S.O.S Repair at €25-35.

Storage & shelf life

29. Shelf life of Honma products?

Sealed: 24-36 months. Opened: 12 months for liquids, 6-12 months for masks/treatments.

30. Storage temperature?

15-25°C. Avoid direct sunlight. Don't store in bathroom (humidity degrades formulations).

Application & technique

31. Can I mix Honma products with non-Honma products?

For maintenance products, yes. For service-time chemistry (smoothing, bleach), stick to within-brand compatibility for predictable results.

32. Can I use Honma on bleached/colored hair?

Yes, with appropriate line — H-S.O.S Capilar or H-Bond Plex for damage protection. HHC home-care for daily maintenance.

33. Is there a specific shampoo to use after Coffee Premium?

HHC Bamboo CocoLux is the standard pairing. Lightweight, sulfate-balanced.

Children, sensitivities, contraindications

34. Can children use Honma products?

Retail HHC products: ages 12+. Professional services (smoothing): 16+ minimum, ideally 18+.

35. Allergic reactions — what to watch for?

Patch test before first use of any new product, especially on the scalp. Watch for: redness, itching, swelling. Discontinue if any develop.

36. Is Honma safe during pregnancy?

Consult your GP or midwife. Most professional smoothing services are avoided during pregnancy. Retail home-care products generally fine.

European market specifics

37. What's the best-selling Honma SKU in Europe?

Coffee Premium Keratin (HSS) for services. Bamboo CocoLux range (HHC) for retail.

38. Does Honma run salon certifications in Europe?

Yes, periodically. Check with your local distributor for certification dates and locations.

39. Where can European clients buy Honma online?

Through authorised distributors. Avoid grey-market or unauthorised resellers — products may be expired or counterfeit.

40. Future Honma launches?

The 2024 catalogue is the current reference. New launches typically announced at the Salao Brasil expo each year.

author: Tomás Costa
content:
Thirty of the most-asked questions about Salvatore Tanino Therapy Exclusive, answered from the 2026 dossier and our salon-side experience working with the system.

About the brand and active

1. What is Tanino?

A polyphenol extracted from acácia-negra (black wattle) bark. Salvatore's base active across the entire Tanino Therapy Exclusive system. See our deep dive.

2. Where is acácia-negra sourced?

Cultivated in southern Brazil. Sustainable forestry — trees regenerate quickly.

3. Is Salvatore cruelty-free?

Yes — the dossier shows the cruelty-free seal alongside the "eu reciclo" sustainability seal.

4. Is Salvatore CPNP-registered in the EU?

Most lines are. Verify SKU-by-SKU with your distributor.

The 7 sub-lines

5. What are the 7 sub-lines?

Hydra Fusion (hydration), Nutri Curl & Waves (curls), Pure Scalp (scalp), Radiant Color (colour protection), Resistance (reconstruction), Revitalize Chemical (chemical detox), Vitality Blond (blonde toning).

6. Which line is the daily/maintenance backbone?

Hydra Fusion. The most-combined line in Mix Therapy recipes. Foundation for most clients.

7. Do I need all 7 lines to start with Salvatore?

No. Start with Hydra Fusion + Resistance + one specialty line (Vitality Blond for blonde clients, Nutri Curl for curl clients, etc.).

TANINOPLASTIA®

8. What is TANINOPLASTIA®?

Salvatore's registered smoothing protocol. Built on TANINO + complementary actives. Formaldehyde-free.

9. How long does TANINOPLASTIA® last?

3-5 months depending on hair type and home-care.

10. Can I do TANINOPLASTIA® on bleached hair?

Yes, with TT Plex layered in. Always strand-test first.

Mix Therapy

11. What is Mix Therapy?

A recipe book of cross-line product combinations. Each recipe targets a specific fibre condition. See our recipe guide.

12. How many Mix Therapy recipes are there?

20+ documented in the dossier across 7 categories.

13. Do I need formal training to use Mix Therapy?

The recipes work from the dossier alone, but Salvatore Educacional certification produces better results and faster service times.

Ionic-Pure & Revitalize Chemical

14. What does Ionic-Pure remove?

Heavy metals from the cortex — copper, iron, calcium, magnesium. Pre-bleach intervention.

15. Is Ionic-Pure the same as anti-residue shampoo?

No. Anti-residue removes surface buildup (sebum, silicone). Ionic-Pure removes mineral residue inside the cortex.

16. How often should home clients use Revitalize Chemical?

Daily for clients with well water or pool exposure. Weekly mask for general maintenance.

TT Plex (Blond Repair System)

17. What's in the TT Plex system?

Three products: Total Injection Repair, Sérum Reconstructor, Fibre Force.

18. How is TT Plex used?

Total Injection Repair goes INTO the bleach. Sérum and Fibre Force used post-service for recovery.

19. Is TT Plex equivalent to Olaplex?

Same category, different chemistry. TT Plex relies on TANINO + Luna Matrix amino acid blend.

Tanino Colors & Colore Gel

20. How many tones does Tanino Colors offer?

60 permanent tones across naturals, ashes, golds, beiges, browns, reds, coppers, plus Special Mix and Super Clareadores (up to level 12).

21. What's special about Tanino Colors?

First permanent colour line with TANINO base. Uses TANINNteract technology for active conduction and Ceril-Protect® film for cuticle alignment.

22. What's Colore Gel?

Newest Salvatore launch — gel-based permanent colour replacing cream base. Micellar penetration, bioadherent shield, 20-minute action.

23. Is Colore Gel ammonia-free?

Yes, 100% ammonia-free.

Application & technique

24. What's the pH range across the lines?

Shampoos: 4.5-5.5. Masks and conditioners: 3.5-4.5. Leave-ins: 3.5-4.5.

25. Can I mix Salvatore products with other brands?

For maintenance products, yes. For TANINOPLASTIA® service or chemical services, stick within Salvatore for predictable Mix Therapy compatibility.

26. What's the maximum flat iron temperature for Vitality Blond?

200°C. Above that, even platinum hair burns and oxidises.

Business & importing

27. What's the wholesale margin for Salvatore in Europe?

Varies by distributor — typically professional margin 45-55% on cost. Premium positioning supports the margin.

28. Minimum order quantity for Salvatore?

Distributor-specific. EU/UK distributors often have moderate MOQs with discount tiers above set thresholds.

29. Does Salvatore run salon certifications in Europe?

Yes — Salvatore Educacional runs certification programmes globally. UK/EU dates announced via the network.

30. Future Salvatore launches?

Colore Gel is the most recent major launch (2026). The 7 Tanino Therapy Exclusive lines are stable. New innovations typically announced at the Salao Brasil expo each year.

title: Importing Brazilian Cosmetics to the EU and UK: 2026 Distributor Checklist
seo_title: Importing Brazilian Cosmetics EU UK — 2026 Distributor Checklist
seo_description: The complete 2026 checklist for distributors importing Brazilian cosmetics to the EU and UK — CPNP, customs, MOQ, margin, brand selection.
excerpt: Importing Brazilian brands to Europe in 2026 — the regulatory, commercial, and operational checklist that distributors actually use.
author: Tomás Costa
content:
Importing Brazilian cosmetics to the EU and UK in 2026 is more straightforward than it was 5 years ago — but the regulatory and operational checklist still trips up new distributors. Here's the complete framework.

Phase 1: Regulatory clearance

1. CPNP registration (EU)

The Cosmetic Products Notification Portal. Every cosmetic placed on the EU market needs CPNP registration. The Responsible Person (RP) handles this.

Most established Brazilian brands (Honma, Salvatore, Brae) have ongoing CPNP registration for their main professional lines. Verify SKU-by-SKU before importing.

2. UK SCPN equivalent

Post-Brexit, the UK has its own Submit Cosmetic Product Notifications system. Separate registration from CPNP. Most brands are running both in parallel.

3. INCI translation

Brazilian INCI lists are in Portuguese. EU/UK require English (and local language depending on member state). Bilingual labels or sticker overlays are standard.

Phase 2: Brand selection

4. Identify your category focus

  • Hair smoothing + repair: Honma Tokyo (heritage), Salvatore (deepest tech)
  • Colour: Salvatore Tanino Colors + Colore Gel
  • Blonde maintenance: Brae Bond Angel, Salvatore Vitality Blond
  • Reconstruction: Brae Revival, Salvatore Resistance
  • Daily home-care retail: Brae Essential, Honma Bamboo CocoLux

5. Brand exclusivity strategy

Most Brazilian brands offer territorial exclusivity to distributors who commit to volume. UK exclusivity rates typically require 6-figure annual commitments. Decide whether you want one brand exclusive or multi-brand portfolio.

6. Brand compatibility

If running multiple brands, ensure they don't compete in the same niche. Honma + Salvatore + Brae is a workable combination because the brands occupy complementary positions.

Phase 3: Commercial setup

7. MOQ negotiations

Typical first-order MOQs:

  • Honma: moderate MOQ, mixed pallet acceptable
  • Salvatore: moderate-to-high MOQ, full container often required for best pricing
  • Brae: moderate MOQ

8. Pricing tiers

Standard pricing tiers:

  • Distributor cost: brand wholesale price (negotiated)
  • Salon wholesale: 1.5-1.8x distributor cost
  • Retail recommended: 2-2.5x salon wholesale

9. Payment terms

First-order: typically 50% deposit + 50% pre-shipment. Established distributors: 30 days net or LC.

Phase 4: Logistics

10. Sea vs air freight

Sea freight from Brazil: 4-6 weeks transit, lower cost, viable for stock-up orders. Air freight: 5-10 days, 4-6x cost, for urgent restocks only.

11. Customs classification

HS codes for cosmetics: typically 3304 series. Different rates for different sub-categories. Work with a customs broker familiar with Brazilian cosmetic imports.

12. Warehouse and stockholding

Cosmetics need climate-controlled storage (15-25°C). Bonded warehouse facilities available in Rotterdam, Antwerp, Felixstowe for EU/UK distribution.

Phase 5: Go-to-market

13. Sales rep network

European salons buy through reps. Build a network of 2-4 reps in each major market, with technical training on the brand chemistry.

14. Salon certification programmes

Brazilian brands offer certification programmes (Honma Brazil, Salvatore Educacional). Bring trainers to Europe 2-3x per year for batched certifications. €450-650 typical per salon technician.

15. Marketing materials translation

Manuals, posters, training decks all need translation. Budget for professional translation of brand materials — bad translations damage premium positioning.

16. Trade show presence

Key European trade shows: Salon Look Madrid, Cosmoprof Bologna, Salon International London. Brand presence at 1-2 of these per year is standard.

Phase 6: Compliance maintenance

17. Adverse event reporting

Both EU and UK require cosmetic adverse event reporting. Set up a complaint logging system from day 1.

18. Product recall protocols

Have a documented recall protocol. Salvatore, Honma, and Brae have all run controlled recalls or batch refreshes — be prepared to do the same.

19. Annual safety assessment review

EU requires periodic Safety Assessor review of formulations. RP coordinates this with the brand.

20. Brexit-specific considerations

UK and EU now have separate regulatory systems. Plan dual stockholding (or routing through UK as EU entry point with separate UK customs clearance).

Common mistakes new distributors make

  1. Importing without CPNP verification — products seized at customs, no recourse.
  2. Mixing salon and retail SKUs in unauthorised channels — damages brand exclusivity, terminates contract.
  3. Cutting corners on translation — manuals in poor English destroy salon trust.
  4. No technical training infrastructure — salons buy once, never reorder.
  5. Underestimating stockholding cost — climate-controlled warehouse fees + insurance + capital tied up.

Who should you talk to in 2026?

For new distributorship inquiries:

  • Honma Brazil — international@honmatokyobrasil.com
  • Salvatore — exportacao@salvatorecosmeticos.com.br
  • Brae — international@braecosmetics.com

(Verify current contact details — these change.)

For distributors already importing Brazilian cosmetics to UK/EU and looking for additional brands: BM Supplier (BBI's distribution partner).
