title: The Brazilian Beauty Ingredient Encyclopedia: A to M
seo_title: Brazilian Beauty Ingredients Encyclopedia A-M — Full Reference
seo_description: Alphabetical encyclopedia of Brazilian beauty actives from A to M — acai, baru, biotin, cocoa, copaiba, etc. Sourced from major brand catalogues.
excerpt: An alphabetical reference to the Brazilian beauty actives that show up across Honma, Salvatore, Brae, and other professional brands. Letters A through M.
author: Tomás Costa
content:
An alphabetical reference to the Brazilian beauty actives that show up across professional brand catalogues. This entry covers letters A through M. (N through Z in the companion article.)

A

Açaí (Euterpe oleracea)

Antioxidant-rich fruit from the Amazon. High in vitamins A, B1, E. Salvatore uses it as the hero active in Vitality Blond for blonde maintenance — replaces yellowing prevention with antioxidant-driven colour stability.

Açafrão oil (saffron)

Carotenoid-rich, antioxidant. Part of the Salvatore Resistance 15-oil complex. High cost limits use to premium lines.

Acácia-negra (Acacia mearnsii)

Black wattle tree native to Australia, cultivated in southern Brazil. Bark is the source of TANINO — Salvatore's proprietary polyphenol active. Sustainable forestry crop.

Algas marinhas (seaweed extract)

Nutrient-dense extract. Used in Brae Revival and Salvatore Pure Scalp. Three-dimensional matrix forms a film that seals other actives during treatment.

Alecrim (rosemary)

Stimulates blood circulation in the scalp, supports hair growth, antioxidant. Part of the Salvatore Pure Scalp 15-herb blend.

Amino acids (cysteine, alanine, arginine, others)

Building blocks of keratin. Penetrate the cortex more efficiently than hydrolyzed keratin due to smaller molecular size. Foundation of Salvatore Luna Matrix (Resistance line).

Argan oil

Standard cosmetic carrier oil. Used as part of multi-oil complexes across Brae Revival, Salvatore Resistance, Honma HHC lines.

B

Bambu (bamboo shoot extract)

Rich in A/B/C vitamins, iron, calcium. Restorative for premature fibre aging. Part of Salvatore Revitalize Chemical and Pure Scalp.

Barbatimão (Stryphnodendron adstringens)

Brazilian Cerrado plant with traditional astringent and healing use. Part of Salvatore Pure Scalp 15-herb blend. Difficult to source outside Brazil through standardised supply chains.

Baru oil

Brazilian Cerrado nut oil, high in oleic acid. Penetrates the cortex like avocado oil but with lighter texture. Used in Salvatore Resistance 15-oil complex.

Biotin (vitamin B7)

Supports keratin production. Improves elasticity and reduces breakage. Used in Brae Essential ampoules and Salvatore Resistance leave-in.

C

Cacau (cocoa) butter

Emollient, melts at body temperature. Used in some Brazilian masks for deep sealing. Less common in professional lines than shea or murumuru.

Café (coffee)

Caffeine and coffee oil. Honma's Coffee Premium Keratin is built around coffee actives. Brazil's coffee production gives Brazilian formulators direct access to pharmaceutical-grade extracts.

Calêndula (calendula)

Anti-inflammatory, soothing. Part of Salvatore Pure Scalp herb blend.

Camomila (chamomile)

Soothing for sensitive scalps. Part of Salvatore Pure Scalp 15-herb blend.

Castor oil (Ricinus communis)

Ricinoleic acid-rich, sealing, dense. Used in Salvatore Vitality Blond mask and across Brae Essential conditioners.

Centella asiática (gotu kola)

Asian herb adopted into Brazilian formulation. Soothing, supports scalp health. Part of Salvatore Pure Scalp blend.

Ceramides

Lipid molecules that form sealing layers on the cuticle. Used in Salvatore Pure Scalp mask (from flaxseed oil) and across other reconstruction lines.

Chia extract

Strengthens fibre elasticity. Used in Salvatore Nutri Curl & Waves shampoo.

Coconut oil (Cocos nucifera)

Penetrating oil with documented cortex absorption. Used in Brae Essential Repairing Fluid and across multiple Brazilian brand oil complexes.

Collagen (hydrolyzed)

Provides structural protein for damaged hair. Used in Salvatore Nutri Curl & Waves and other reconstruction-focused formulations.

Confrei (comfrey)

Soothing scalp herb. Part of Salvatore Pure Scalp 15-herb blend.

Copaíba

Amazon tree resin. Anti-inflammatory, used in some Brazilian scalp lines. Less common than the broader 15-herb formulations.

D

D-Panthenol (pro-vitamin B5)

Long-lasting moisturiser, ubiquitous across the Brazilian professional category. Used in Brae Essential (all SKUs), Salvatore leave-ins, Honma HHC.

Dimethicone and silicones

Cuticle smoothing agents. The "noble silicones" mentioned in Salvatore and Honma formulations are higher-grade silicone blends with better wash-out profiles than legacy silicones.

E

Elastin

Structural protein. Restores elasticity to damaged fibre. Used in Salvatore Nutri Curl & Waves mask.

F

Film-forming polymers (Fix agents)

Synthetic polymers that form a flexible film on fibre. Provide hold for curls and protect against humidity. Used in Salvatore Day-After spray.

Flaxseed (linhaça) oil

Omega 3/6, ceramides. Used in Salvatore Pure Scalp mask and Salvatore Vitality Blond.

G

Glycerin

Universal hydrating humectant. Foundational in most Brazilian shampoo and mask formulations.

Glycerina + Colágeno blend

Named active combination in Salvatore Nutri Curl & Waves — hydration + structural protein. Specific to the curl line formulation.

H

Hamamélis (witch hazel)

Astringent, anti-inflammatory. Part of Salvatore Pure Scalp blend.

Homosalato (Homosalate)

UVB filter. Used in Salvatore Vitality Blond Leave-In Sérum — protects bleached fibre from sun-driven oxidation.

Hortelã (mint)

Cooling, refreshing scalp active. Part of Salvatore Pure Scalp herb blend.

Hyaluronic acid

Polysaccharide that binds up to 1,000x its weight in water. Brae built the entire Essential line around it. See our dedicated guide.

Hydrolyzed keratin

Broken-down keratin protein. Penetrates the cortex more easily than intact keratin. Used in Brae Essential ampoules, Salvatore Resistance, Honma HHT/HHC lines.

I

Ionic-Pure

Salvatore's metal-removal technology. Identifies, captures, and expels heavy metals from the cortex. See our deep dive.

J

Jojoba oil

Wax ester profile mimics natural sebum. Part of Salvatore Radiant Color Radiant Prism bioester complex.

K

Karité (shea) butter

Emollient, sealing, nutrition. Used in Brae Bond Angel and across Salvatore Pure Scalp / Vitality Blond / Resistance mask formulations.

Keratin (hydrolyzed)

Lower molecular weight than intact keratin. Penetrates the fibre, restores structure and elasticity. Used in Salvatore Pure Scalp mask and across reconstruction lines.

L

Luna Matrix

Salvatore's registered amino acid blend (cysteine + alanine + arginine). Foundation of the Resistance line for reconstruction.

M

Macadâmia oil

Palmitoleic acid-rich, sebum-mimetic. Used across Brae Revival, Salvatore Resistance, Brae Essential Oil Blend.

Mango (manga) extract and butter

Hydrating, emollient, remineralising. Antioxidant. Used in Salvatore Radiant Color line.

Mentol (menthol)

Vasodilator. Increases scalp blood flow when applied. Anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial. Salvatore Pure Scalp shampoo's hero active alongside rosemary.

Murumuru butter

Higher melting point than shea, denser sealing. Amazon-sourced from murumuru palm. Used in Salvatore Nutri Curl & Waves for curl sealing.

Myrrh oil

Antioxidant, traditionally healing. Part of the Salvatore Resistance 15-oil complex.

Continued in part 2

For letters N through Z, see the Brazilian Beauty Ingredient Encyclopedia: N to Z (companion article).

seo_description: Ten Honma Tokyo products worth stocking in a European salon — Coffee Premium Keratin, H-Bond Plex, H-S.O.S Capilar, more. Ranked and explained.
excerpt: Not every Honma product makes sense for a European salon. These ten do — ranked by service-day demand and retail attach.
author: Sofia Almeida
content:
Honma Tokyo's catalogue runs to 90+ SKUs across five product lines. Not all of them belong in a European salon. These ten do — ranked by service-day demand, retail attach, and the kind of recurring revenue they generate.

1. Coffee Premium Keratin (HSS)

The flagship smoothing protocol. Formaldehyde-free, coffee-rich formula that delivers a stable smoothing service with proven Brazilian heritage. The service most likely to drive new clients to your door.

2. H-Bond Plex (HHT)

Mixed into bleach during lifting to protect disulfide bonds. Direct competitor to international plex systems, at a lower professional cost. The product that converts your bleach service into a premium tier.

3. H-S.O.S Capilar (HHT)

The 5-step rescue protocol. A premium in-salon treatment for clients walking in with severe damage — bleach history, chemical cuts, or progressive heat damage. Ticket-builder.

4. Bamboo CocoLux Fusion (HHC)

The daily-use line for retail attach. Light formulation, good for fine to medium hair, accessible price point. The line that goes home in 3 out of 5 client bags.

5. H-S.O.S Repair (HHC home care)

The retail companion to H-S.O.S Capilar. Clients who get the in-salon treatment buy this for the 4-6 weeks between visits. Subscription-style revenue.

6. H-One Neutralizing (HCP)

The pH reset after colour services. Most salons skip this step. Salons that don't see materially better colour retention. Worth the 5 minutes added to the service.

7. HCP Toning range

For salons offering colour services, the Honma toning line completes the offering. Lower cost than European house tones, comparable result on darker bases.

8. HPF Thermal Protection finishers

Every smoothing client and every colour client needs daily thermal protection. The HPF line is the retail attach you offer at checkout — high margin, low resistance.

9. H-Brush range (Tools)

Electric brushes are the most-requested device in 2026. The H-Brush range is Honma's professional-tier offering — for salon use and for retail to clients who want salon-quality results at home.

10. Honma Pro Finish flat iron (Tools)

Every smoothing service needs a flat iron tuned for the chemistry. Honma's pro flat iron is designed around their own smoothing protocols. Buy the device alongside the chemistry.

What didn't make the list

Sustainability-focused products (P-Life packaging line, refill kits) are valuable but not service-driving. Specialty colour ranges beyond the toning core fit only some salon books.

title: Salvatore: 7 Innovations Worth Knowing About
seo_title: Salvatore Tanino Therapy — 7 Key Innovations
seo_description: Seven Salvatore innovations changing professional hair care — TANINO, TANINOPLASTIA®, Luna Matrix, Ionic-Pure, Radiant Prism, TT Plex, Colore Gel.
excerpt: Salvatore's seven patented innovations — from TANINO polyphenol to Colore Gel deposit system. The technologies that separate them from generic Brazilian brands.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
Salvatore's Tanino Therapy Exclusive system isn't built on one technology. It's built on seven distinct innovations, each addressing a specific failure mode in professional hair chemistry. Here's the rundown.

1. TANINO — the polyphenol base active

Extracted from acácia-negra bark, TANINO is the polyphenol that earned Salvatore its TANINOPLASTIA® registered protocol. Antioxidant, protein-binding, increases the adherence of other formulation actives. Foundation of all 7 sub-lines.

2. TANINOPLASTIA® — registered smoothing protocol

The smoothing service built around TANINO. Works through polyphenol-keratin affinity, not through breaking and reforming disulfide bonds. Lower toxicity than legacy Brazilian smoothing chemistry. Survived European regulatory scrutiny that took down formaldehyde-class methods.

3. Luna Matrix — reconstruction amino acid blend

Cysteine + alanine + arginine. The reconstruction blend in the Resistance line. Each amino acid plays a distinct role — cysteine reforms disulfide bonds, alanine fills smaller cortex fissures, arginine supports the bonding process.

4. Ionic-Pure — heavy metal removal

The technology that removes copper, iron, calcium from the cortex before chemical services. Solves the unspoken problem of why bleach services fail unpredictably in clients with well water or pool exposure. Used in the Revitalize Chemical line.

5. Radiant Prism — colour protection bioester complex

Five-source vegetable bioester (rice, sunflower, olive, palm, jojoba) that seals cuticles around fresh pigment. Powers the Radiant Color line. Extends colour retention significantly versus standard colour-safe shampoo systems.

6. TT Plex — Blond Repair System

Three-product bond-protection system (Total Injection Repair + Sérum Reconstructor + Fibre Force). Mixed INTO the bleach, not separate pre/post treatments. Direct competitor to international plex systems with native compatibility across the Salvatore line.

7. Colore Gel — gel-based deposit system

The newest innovation. Translucent polymeric gel replaces cream base for permanent colour. Faster oxidation, higher penetration via micelle nano-spheres, bioadherent shield prevents fade. 20-minute action time, 100% ammonia-free.

Why this matters strategically

Most Brazilian professional brands have one or two named technologies. Salvatore has seven registered or named innovations — each anchoring a different sub-line. That depth is what makes the brand defensible against generic Brazilian competition and credible against European house brands.

title: 8 Ingredients You Only Find in Brazilian Hair Care
seo_title: 8 Brazilian Hair Care Ingredients — TANINO, Murumuru, Pracaxi, more
seo_description: Eight active ingredients used in Brazilian hair care that European brands don't have access to — TANINO, Murumuru, Pracaxi, Baru, Açaí, and more.
excerpt: Eight actives Brazilian brands use that European houses can't reliably source. The botanical edge that explains why these brands feel different.
author: Tomás Costa
content:
European hair care has access to global ingredients. But there's a tier of actives — Brazilian Cerrado plants, Amazonian oils, sub-tropical extracts — that Brazilian brands work with as routine while European houses treat as exotic. Here are eight that show up across Honma, Salvatore, and Brae.

1. TANINO (acácia-negra polyphenol)

Sourced from acácia-negra (black wattle) bark cultivated in southern Brazil. Polyphenol with high protein affinity. Salvatore built TANINOPLASTIA® around it. Not a generic "tannin" — a specific concentration and extraction.

2. Pracaxi oil

From the Amazon rainforest. Highest behenic acid content known in commercial cosmetic oils — directly anti-frizz and emollient. Used in Salvatore's Resistance 15-oil complex.

3. Murumuru butter

From the murumuru palm of the Amazon. Higher melting point than shea, denser sealing capacity. Key active in Salvatore Nutri Curl & Waves for sealing curls without weighing them down.

4. Baru oil

Brazilian Cerrado nut oil, high in oleic acid. Penetrates the cortex like avocado oil but lighter texture. Used in Salvatore Resistance.

5. Açaí extract

Antioxidant-rich, vitamin A/B1/E concentrated. Used in Salvatore Vitality Blond as the lead active for blonde maintenance — replaces yellowing prevention with antioxidant-driven colour stability.

6. Barbatimão

Brazilian Cerrado plant with traditional astringent and healing use. Part of the Salvatore Pure Scalp 15-herb blend. Difficult to source outside Brazil through standardised supply chains.

7. Açafrão (saffron) oil

Carotenoid-rich, antioxidant. Part of the Salvatore Resistance 15-oil complex. Used at concentrations that would be cost-prohibitive in European-tier products.

8. Coffee derivatives

Caffeine and coffee oil are used in Honma's flagship Coffee Premium Keratin as part of the smoothing chemistry. Brazil being the world's largest coffee producer makes pharmaceutical-grade coffee actives directly available to Brazilian formulators.

Why this matters

You can buy argan oil anywhere. Pracaxi, murumuru, and baru require dedicated Amazon supply chains. The Brazilian brands that work with these actives have decades of formulation experience and sourcing relationships European houses can't replicate quickly.

This is the botanical edge that explains why a Brazilian Tanino Therapy treatment feels distinct from a European mass-market mask. It's not marketing differentiation — it's actually different chemistry.

title: Brazilian Curl Care Compared: Salvatore Nutri Curl vs Honma vs Brae

excerpt: Curl care is where Brazilian formulation really shines. Three Brazilian approaches compared head-to-head for curls 2A through 4C.
author: Sofia Almeida
content:
Curl care is the category where Brazilian formulation actually outperforms European house brands. Brazil has both the population (~50% of women have curls or waves) and the climate (humidity) that forced formulators to engineer real solutions.

Three brands, three different approaches. Here's the comparison.

Salvatore Nutri Curl & Waves

The most curl-specific line of the three. Engineered for 2A through 4C curl patterns. Five products including a Day-After spray that re-activates curl memory without re-washing.

Active stack

  • Murumuru butter — denser sealing than shea
  • Hydrolyzed collagen + elastin (mask)
  • Castor oil (conditioner)
  • Omegas 6/7/9 (leave-in)
  • D-Panthenol + glycerin + film-forming polymers (Day-After spray)

Standout feature

The Day-After spray is the giveaway. Most curl lines stop at wash-day products. Salvatore engineered a refresher specifically for the day after wash, when curl shape degrades from sleep and humidity.

Honma — no curl-specific line, but cross-line options

Honma's catalogue doesn't include a dedicated curl line in the way Salvatore does. Curl-pattern clients are typically routed through HHC Bamboo CocoLux Fusion for daily care, with HHT H-S.O.S Capilar or H-S.O.S Repair for damaged curls.

What Honma does well

If a curl client is also damaged (chemical history, mechanical breakage), Honma's reconstruction-led approach with H-S.O.S Capilar gives better fibre recovery than a pure curl line would. But for healthy curls needing daily care, Honma is less specialised.

Brae — Essential + Divine for curl-friendly daily care

Brae's catalogue mentions Divine as the line "for intense hydration with anti-frizz action" — positioned as the curl-friendly daily care. Essential handles lighter hydration needs.

What Brae does well

Hyaluronic acid in shampoo is genuinely useful for curls — high water retention without buildup. Essential + Divine pair as the daily/intensive duo for curl maintenance.

title: 6 Myths About Brazilian Smoothing, Debunked
seo_title: Brazilian Smoothing Myths Debunked — Formaldehyde, Damage, Cost
seo_description: Six persistent myths about Brazilian smoothing — formaldehyde fear, irreversible damage, ruined curls, blonde incompatibility — debunked with sources.
excerpt: Brazilian smoothing accumulated a decade of bad press. Some of it was deserved. Most of it now applies to chemistry that no professional Brazilian brand actually uses anymore.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
Brazilian smoothing accumulated a decade of bad press in Europe. Some of it was deserved — the early formaldehyde-heavy formulations did damage. But most of the current narrative applies to chemistry that no professional Brazilian brand actually uses anymore.

Here are the six most persistent myths, with what's actually true in 2026.

Myth 1: "All Brazilian smoothing contains formaldehyde"

False. Honma Coffee Premium Keratin is formaldehyde-free. Salvatore TANINOPLASTIA® is formaldehyde-free — built on the TANINO polyphenol instead. Most professional Brazilian brands moved away from formaldehyde 5-7 years ago because of European regulation, not just consumer fear.

What to actually check

Ask the salon for the product label. CPNP-registered products available in the EU disclose ingredients. Formaldehyde, methylene glycol, and formaldehyde-releasers must be declared.

Myth 2: "Smoothing destroys your hair forever"

Depends on the chemistry. Old formaldehyde-based smoothing did permanent cortex damage. Modern Brazilian smoothing (TANINOPLASTIA®, modern keratin systems with bond protection) is reversible — when you stop the maintenance, the natural curl returns over 4-6 months.

Myth 3: "Brazilian smoothing ruins curls"

Only if you don't want curls back. Smoothing is a reversible service in modern chemistry. Many curl wearers do Brazilian smoothing for transitional periods (post-pregnancy, post-medical, for a wedding) and return to natural curl after.

For wearers wanting curl maintenance after smoothing, lines like Salvatore Nutri Curl & Waves are formulated to maintain curl elasticity during the smoothing recovery period.

Myth 4: "You can't bleach over Brazilian smoothing"

False, but with caveats. You can bleach over modern Brazilian smoothing IF you use bond protection (Honma H-Bond Plex, Salvatore TT Plex). Without bond protection, yes, you'll see breakage at the smoothed sections.

Myth 5: "Brazilian smoothing is just cheaper European keratin"

False. Brazilian smoothing is a distinct chemistry category with different active classes. European keratin (à la Kerastase) typically focuses on hydrolyzed keratin in masks. Brazilian smoothing combines polyphenols, amino acids, vegetable oils, and specific application protocols that don't translate.

Myth 6: "All Brazilian brands are the same"

Demonstrably false. Honma is heritage-led with Japanese-Brazilian chemistry. Salvatore is the deepest tech platform with 7 distinct sub-lines. Brae is focused on reconstruction and hydration with clean line architecture. Each one differentiates on specific actives and approach.

What's actually worth worrying about

Smoothing services run by untrained technicians, with off-brand chemistry, no porosity testing, and no bond protection on bleach overlap. That's the real risk profile. Not the brand category.

title: Bond Protection Compared: H-Bond Plex vs TT Plex vs Bond Angel
seo_title: Bond Protection Systems Compared — Brazilian Plex Guide
seo_description: Three Brazilian bond protection systems compared — Honma H-Bond Plex, Salvatore TT Plex, Brae Bond Angel. How they work, when to use each.
excerpt: The three Brazilian answers to Olaplex. Different mechanisms, different protocols, different price points. Here's how to choose.
author: Sofia Almeida
content:
Olaplex made bond protection a global category. Brazil has three serious answers. Here's how they actually compare.

Honma H-Bond Plex

Part of the HHT line. Mixed into the bleach formula during application. Protects disulfide bonds during the lift phase.

Mechanism

Standard plex-class chemistry. Bond-protective monomers that bind to disulfide bridges in the cortex during the bleach reaction. Slows the bond breakage rate.

Best for

Salons running Honma colour or smoothing — H-Bond Plex integrates with the rest of the HHT line for damaged hair recovery.

Salvatore TT Plex (Blond Repair System)

Three-product system: Total Injection Repair + Sérum Reconstructor + Fibre Force. Total Injection Repair goes INTO the bleach mixture.

Mechanism

The dossier illustrates the chemistry: persulfates in the bleach formula cleave disulfide bridges; Total Injection Repair, mixed into the bleach, contributes amino acids (cysteine, glycine, glutamine, alanine) that re-form bridges in real time.

Best for

Salons running Salvatore TANINOPLASTIA® or working extensively in blonde. The 3-product system is the most thorough of the three.

Brae Bond Angel (Blonde Repair line)

Different positioning — Brae's Bond Angel is the post-service maintenance line for bleached hair, not in-service bond protection.

Mechanism

Protein blend + amino acids + shea butter in shampoo, conditioner, mask, leave-in. Reconstructs and reinforces fibre post-bleach.

Best for

Daily home care for bleached and blonde clients. Pairs with H-Bond Plex or TT Plex used at service-time — the combination is stronger than either alone.

H-Bond Plex (simpler, lower stock cost). Or just use Bond Angel post-service alone.

If you do 5+ bleach services per week and want premium positioning

TT Plex Salvatore. The 3-product system charges more, delivers more visible bond protection during the service, and produces fewer disasters on high-lift work.

If you want maximum retail attach

title: How to Choose Your Brazilian Smoothing: A Decision Guide
seo_title: Brazilian Smoothing Decision Guide — How to Choose 2026
seo_description: Decision tree for choosing a Brazilian smoothing service — hair type, history, climate, budget, maintenance commitment all factored in.
excerpt: Not every Brazilian smoothing is for every client. Six questions to answer before you book — and what each answer implies.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
Brazilian smoothing isn't one service. It's a family of services with different chemistries, different commitment levels, and different fit profiles. Before you book — or before you recommend to a client — work through these six questions.

Question 1: What's your hair history?

If your hair is virgin (no chemical service in 12+ months)

You have the widest range of options. Both Honma Coffee Premium and Salvatore TANINOPLASTIA® will perform predictably. Lower-risk service, more visible result.

If you have colour but no bleach

Both Honma and Salvatore work. Salvatore TANINOPLASTIA® edges out slightly because the polyphenol chemistry doesn't compete with permanent colour pigments for cortex space.

If you have bleach or highlights

Salvatore TANINOPLASTIA® + TT Plex layered in is the safest path. Honma works too with H-Bond Plex protection. NEVER do Brazilian smoothing on bleached hair without bond protection in the mix.

If your hair is bleached and porous

STOP. Do a strand test first. If the strand snaps after the test, the fibre isn't a candidate for smoothing right now. Run Salvatore Resistance or Brae Revival for 6-8 weeks first to rebuild mass, then re-test.

Question 2: What's your curl pattern?

2A-2C (waves)

Smoothing here is more about volume reduction and frizz control than curl elimination. Honma Coffee Premium or Plastica de Argila — both deliver a polished result without aggressive straightening.

3A-3C (curls)

Most reversible category. Smoothing typically lasts 4-5 months. After fade, natural curl returns. Salvatore TANINOPLASTIA® preserves curl elasticity better during the maintenance phase.

4A-4C (coils/tight curls)

Most permanent-feeling result. Curl pattern memory takes longer to return. Honma Coffee Premium for maximum service longevity, Salvatore for milder approach that re-emerges as curl naturally.

Question 3: Your climate

High humidity (London, Lisbon, Mediterranean coast)

Anti-frizz performance matters more than perfect straightening. Smoothing + retail home care matter equally. Stock the smoothing service WITH the home-care line (Brae Divine for anti-frizz, Salvatore Hydra Fusion for hydration).

Dry climate (Madrid, Berlin, Paris in summer)

Hydration retention matters more than humidity control. Salvatore Hydra Fusion as the home-care backbone. Smoothing duration tends to be longer in drier climates.

Question 4: Maintenance commitment

"I want to do this once and forget"

Honma Coffee Premium with full HHC home-care line. Highest durability of the three options, designed for low-touch maintenance.

"I'm willing to do home-care 3x per week"

Salvatore TANINOPLASTIA® with Mix Therapy custom protocols. The most personalised result, requires the most consistent maintenance.

"I want flexibility"

Brazilian smoothing isn't the right category. Consider Brazilian curl care lines (Salvatore Nutri Curl & Waves) for curl maintenance without permanent shape change.

Question 5: Budget

Entry-level (€150-200)

Honma Coffee Premium. Best service-cost-to-result ratio in 2026 Europe.

Mid-tier (€200-300)

Salvatore TANINOPLASTIA® + Ionic-Pure pre-chemistry detox. Better safety margin, longer-lasting result.

Premium (€300+)

Salvatore TANINOPLASTIA® + TT Plex + Mix Therapy custom protocol + complete Tanino Therapy Exclusive home-care line. The full salon-grade experience.

Question 6: Salon experience

Is the technician certified?

Brazilian smoothing requires training. Salvatore Educacional and Honma Brazil run certified technician programmes. Ask the salon — they should be able to name the brand certification.

How long has the salon been doing Brazilian smoothing?

Less than 6 months: be cautious. Brazilian smoothing has learning-curve service failures. 12+ months of experience produces consistent results.

Quick decision tree

Virgin hair + want long-lasting + budget-friendly → Honma Coffee Premium

Coloured hair + want premium safety + willing to maintain → Salvatore TANINOPLASTIA® + Mix Therapy

Bleached hair + want any smoothing → Salvatore TT Plex + TANINOPLASTIA® (or do not smooth)

Curly hair + want reversibility → Salvatore (better curl recovery post-fade)

Humid climate + frizz priority → Honma Coffee Premium + Brae Divine home care

title: Brae Essential Mask: When to Use It and How to Get Results
seo_title: Brae Essential Mask — When and How to Use Guide
seo_description: Brae Essential Mask with hyaluronic acid and amino acids for hydration and deep repair. Twice-weekly use, 10-minute pause. Full how-to.
excerpt: A mask isn't a conditioner. Brae Essential Mask runs an intensive ten-minute hydration cycle that the daily conditioner can't deliver — here's why and when.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
Conditioners run a minute. Masks run ten. That difference is the formulation's entire purpose. Brae Essential Mask is engineered for the deeper penetration that only a longer pause allows — and used correctly, it's the most powerful hydration step in the Essential lineup.

What it is

An intensive repairing treatment that promotes prolonged hydration and protection of the hair fibre. Leaves hair stronger, hydrated, softer, and shinier.

What's in it

  • Hyaluronic acid — High hydration power, strengthens strands, protects the hair fibre, repairs split ends.
  • Blend of amino acids — Strengthens hair structure, repairs damage, increases strength and shine.
  • Panthenol (pro-vitamin B5) — Long-lasting moisturizer, prevents damage, adds shine, increases thickness, reduces split ends.

How to use it

  1. Wash hair with Essential Shampoo. Rinse.
  2. Remove excess moisture with a towel (the mask penetrates better into damp, not soaking, hair).
  3. Apply to length and ends, strand by strand if possible.
  4. Leave on for 10 minutes.
  5. Rinse thoroughly with warm or cold water.
  6. Finish with leave-in or oil blend if desired.

Frequency: Up to 2 times per week.

Why 10 minutes matters

The cuticle scales need time to lift, allow the actives to penetrate, and re-close. Hyaluronic acid in particular needs the longer pause — its hydrating film depends on full saturation of the cuticle layer, not surface contact.

Skip the pause and you've used the mask as an expensive conditioner. Use the pause and the mask delivers what the conditioner can't.

Where it sits in the capillary schedule

The FAQ places the Essential mask in the hydration stage of a capillary schedule. If you're rotating treatments (hydration → nutrition → reconstruction), Essential Mask is your hydration product.

For nutrition you'd rotate to Brae Divine. For reconstruction you'd rotate to Brae Revival or Bond Angel. The Essential mask alone, used every wash, eventually under-delivers because the fibre needs the other two stages too.

The mask + oil blend combination

The FAQ confirms you can add the Essential Oil Blend into the mask to enhance the result. The technique:

  1. In the palm of your hand, mix a portion of the mask with 2-3 drops of Oil Blend.
  2. Apply the mixture to length and ends.
  3. Pause 10 minutes as normal.
  4. Rinse thoroughly.

This pulls the mask from pure hydration toward hydration + nutrition — useful for fibre that needs both.

The mask + ampoule combination (Power Treatment)

The Brae FAQ also confirms you can mix Essential ampoules into the Essential mask: "this mixture will enhance the delivery of the benefits of the mask through a deeper and more effective result for the hair."

The protocol:

  1. Wash with Essential Shampoo.
  2. In a bowl, combine 4ml ampoule with a portion of Essential Mask.
  3. Apply to length and ends.
  4. Pause 10 minutes.
  5. Rinse thoroughly.

For severely damaged fibre, use the Anti-Breakage Ampoule in the mix. For dehydrated but intact fibre, use the Intense Repair Ampoule.

Sizes

  • 200g — Retail. Lasts about 8-10 weeks at 2x/week use.
  • 500g — Professional / back bar. Bulk service size.

Who it's for

All hair types, especially those that suffer from dryness and dullness. Per the Brae FAQ, also suitable for colored hair, and can be alternated with Soul Color products for colour protection.

For severely damaged hair, the Anti-Breakage Ampoule should accompany or replace the mask in the rotation. The mask alone is hydration-focused and can't reconstruct broken bonds.

Source: Brae Manual Técnico 2024.

title: Brae Essential Oil Blend: Thermal Protection from Avocado, Rosehip, Sunflower, Macadamia
seo_title: Brae Essential Oil Blend — Thermal Protection Guide
seo_description: Brae Essential Oil Blend combines hyaluronic acid with avocado, rosehip, sunflower, macadamia. Thermal protection and lipid replacement for daily use.
excerpt: A finishing oil isn't a finisher — it's a daily lipid replacement that doubles as thermal shield. Here's how Brae's combines four oils with hyaluronic acid.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
European hair care treats finishing oils as cosmetic — apply for shine, end of story. Brazilian salon-grade brands treat them as functional — daily lipid replacement, thermal protection, and cumulative cuticle sealing.

Brae's Essential Oil Blend sits in the second category. The formula combines hyaluronic acid with a four-oil complex specifically tuned for the role of daily protector.

The composition

Active stack:

  • Hyaluronic acid — High hydration power, strengthens the strands, protects the hair fibre, repairs split ends.
  • Oil blend — Complex of avocado, rosehip, sunflower, and macadamia oils. Nourishes and repairs, creates a film around the hair that prevents moisture loss, keeping the hair hydrated longer.

Volume: 60ml.

Use: Daily, on damp or dry hair.

The four oils, by role

Avocado oil

One of the highest-penetration oils in cosmetic formulation. Avocado oil contains oleic acid (a small fatty acid that passes through the cuticle) and lecithin (a natural emollient). It penetrates the cortex, not just coats the surface — making it one of the few oils that actually treats the fibre from inside.

Rosehip oil

Rich in linoleic acid (omega-6) and retinol-class natural vitamin A. The combination supports cellular regeneration in tissue and antioxidant protection in fibre. In hair, rosehip is the anti-oxidation arm of the blend — protecting colour and structural proteins from UV and environmental damage.

Sunflower oil

High in vitamin E (tocopherols), light texture, doesn't weigh down fine hair. Sunflower is the carrier oil of the blend — it makes the heavier oils application-friendly and provides antioxidant support.

Macadamia oil

One of the closest-to-skin-sebum oil profiles in nature. Macadamia is high in palmitoleic acid, which the fibre readily absorbs and which mimics natural sebum behaviour. It's the sealing arm of the blend — closing cuticles and reducing porosity.

Thermal protection — how it works

The Brae description names the product's thermal protection function explicitly. The mechanism: the oil film deposits on the fibre, creates a hydrophobic barrier, and dissipates heat across the surface during blow-drying or flat-ironing.

This isn't optional protection. Heat damage occurs above 150°C — flat irons routinely run 180-220°C. Without a thermal barrier, the cuticle scorches and the protein in the cortex denatures permanently. With the Oil Blend, the heat distribution is more even and the fibre tolerates higher temperatures with less damage.

How to use it

Apply a few drops of Oil Blend Essential to the palm of your hands and spread over damp or dry hair. Massage and finish as you wish.

For damp hair (pre-heat): apply, then blow-dry or flat-iron. Thermal protection role.

For dry hair (finish): apply minimal amount to ends. Shine and frizz control role.

The mask + oil blend combination

The FAQ explicitly endorses mixing the Oil Blend into the Essential Mask: "Yes, you can add Oil Blend from Essential to enhance the result."

This pulls the mask from pure hydration toward hydration + nutrition combined. Useful when:

  • The fibre feels dehydrated AND stripped of lipids
  • You want a stronger sealing finish after the mask treatment
  • Coloured or chemically treated hair where the cuticle has gaps to fill

Daily use cadence

The Essential Oil Blend is one of the daily-use products in the line (along with shampoo, conditioner, repairing fluid, anti-breakage fluid, and leave-in). The mask and ampoules are the 2x/week products.

Who it's for

All hair types. Lighter texture than the heavier oils (argan or coconut alone) — won't overload fine hair. Heavier than serum-class products — provides genuine lipid replacement, not just visual shine.

Particularly valuable for: bleached or colour-treated hair (cuticle gaps to fill), curly hair (constant lipid loss along curve), pre-heat-styling routines (thermal protection), travel (one product covers shine + protection + repair).

title: Brae Essential Repairing Fluid vs Anti-Breakage Fluid: Two Sprays, Two Jobs
seo_title: Brae Essential Repairing vs Anti-Breakage Fluid Comparison
seo_description: Brae Essential ships two leave-in sprays — Repairing Fluid for daily hydration, Anti-Breakage Fluid for active breakage. How to choose.
excerpt: Two leave-in sprays that look almost identical and do completely different things. Here's the difference.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
Brae's Essential line ships two spray-format leave-ins side by side — the Essential Repairing Fluid and the Essential Anti-Breakage Fluid. The packaging is nearly identical. The chemistry isn't.

Pick the wrong one and you'll get a perfectly acceptable result that's not the result you needed. Pick correctly and the daily routine actually solves the problem.

Essential Repairing Fluid (260ml)

For: Daily use, all hair types. Prolonged hydration and repair.

Description: Hair repair fluid with thermal protection. Promotes prolonged hydration, hair repair, and protection against external aggressions. Result: soft, silky, shiny hair.

Key benefits:

  • Prolonged hydration and repair
  • Protection against thermal and external aggressions
  • Softness, shine, and malleability of the strands

Actives:

  • Hyaluronic acid — intense moisture, fibre protection, split-end repair
  • Coconut oil — nutrition and intense repair
  • Panthenol — prolonged hydration, prevents damage, increases thickness

How to use: Shake. Apply to damp or dry hair, gently massaging along the entire length. Finish as desired.

Frequency: Daily use.

Essential Anti-Breakage Fluid (260ml)

For: Severely damaged, brittle, breaking fibre. Up to 3x per week.

Description: Enriched with a blend of amino acids, proteins, panthenol, and coconut oil. Replenishes proteins in the deeper layers of the hair, rebuilds brittle strands, seals the cuticles, strengthens the structure, increases resistance, repairs damage from chemical processes and thermal tools.

Key benefits:

  • Prevents breakage
  • Moisturizes the strands
  • Brilliance
  • Visible results on the first application
  • Thermal protection

Actives:

  • Amino acid blend — strengthens structure, repair, treatment
  • Proteins — replenish cortex protein, repair brittle hair, replenish mass, thermal protection
  • Panthenol — long-lasting hydration
  • Coconut oil — nutrition and repair

How to use: Shake. Apply to damp or dry hair, gently massaging along the length. Finish as desired.

Frequency: Up to 3 times per week.

The decision tree

Choose Repairing Fluid if:

  • Hair needs daily hydration and thermal protection
  • Fibre is dry, dull, slightly damaged
  • You're using heat styling tools regularly
  • No active breakage occurring
  • You want a daily, no-think leave-in

Choose Anti-Breakage Fluid if:

  • Hair is actively breaking under brushing or styling
  • Post-bleach, post-chemical, post-cut
  • Strands are visibly fragile
  • Fibre has lost elasticity (stretches and breaks instead of springing back)
  • You need visible reinforcement after the first wash

Why hyaluronic acid is in one but not the other

The Repairing Fluid carries hyaluronic acid as a hero active — the formula is hydration-focused, with repair as a secondary benefit.

The Anti-Breakage Fluid carries amino acids and proteins as hero actives — the formula is reconstruction-focused, with hydration as a secondary benefit via panthenol and coconut oil.

Different problems need different chemistry. Brae could have made one universal fluid that does both jobs at half strength. They chose two specialised fluids at full strength instead.

Can you alternate between them?

Yes. For combined damage + dehydration: use Anti-Breakage Fluid 2-3x per week and Repairing Fluid on the other days. This builds a cumulative reconstruction + hydration schedule without protein overload.

The 60ml travel sizes of both products make this rotation easy to maintain at home and on travel.

Where they sit in the line

Both products are finishers — used after the wash and conditioner, not as treatments. The treatments are the masks and ampoules. The fluids are the daily maintenance layer between treatments.

The full cadence for a damaged-hair client:

  • Daily: Essential Shampoo + Conditioner + Anti-Breakage Fluid (after wash) + Oil Blend (pre-heat or finish)
  • 1-2x/week: Essential Mask
  • 1-2x/week: Essential Anti-Breakage Ampoule

That's a complete five-product routine using only the Essential line.

Source: Brae Manual Técnico 2024.

title: Brae Lines Compared: Essential vs Divine vs Revival vs Bond Angel
seo_title: Brae Lines Compared — Which One Is Right for You
seo_description: Brae makes Essential, Divine, Revival, Bond Angel and more. Each line targets a specific need. Full decision guide based on Brae's own FAQ.
excerpt: Brae's line architecture isn't decorative. Each line targets a distinct fibre problem. Here's how to know which one belongs on your shelf.
author: Sofia Almeida
content:
Brae makes too many lines to memorise. Walk into a salon that retails the brand and you'll see Essential, Revival, Bond Angel (Blonde Repair), Divine, Soul Color, Defense, and others. Without a map, the choice paralysis sets in.

The good news: Brae's own technical manual draws explicit comparisons in the FAQ section. Here's the map.

The five core lines

Essential — Hydration + Repair

Built on: Hyaluronic acid + amino acids + panthenol.

For: All hair types, especially dry and dull.

Job: Prolonged hydration and moderate repair.

13 SKUs. Shampoo, Conditioner, Mask, two Ampoules (Repair + Anti-Breakage), Oil Blend, two sprays (Repairing Fluid + Anti-Breakage Fluid).

Divine — Intense Hydration + Anti-Frizz

For: Hair that needs deeper hydration than Essential delivers, plus active frizz control.

Job: "Intense hydration and has anti-frizz action" (per Brae FAQ, comparing directly to Essential).

Pick Divine over Essential when frizz is the dominant complaint or hydration needs are extreme.

Revival — Reconstruction for Extremely Damaged Hair

Built on: Butter blend (Shorea + Shea), seaweed extract, vegetable oil blend, wheat/almond/oat protein, amino acids, panthenol.

For: Chemically treated hair with porous, extremely damaged strands.

Job: Immediate reconstruction. Rebuilds all layers of the fibre.

15 SKUs. Shampoo (250ml + 1L + 60g travel), Conditioner (same sizes), Mask (200g + 500g + 60g travel), Ampoule (13ml), Leave-In, Intense Shine Spray, Gorgeous Shine Oil.

Bond Angel / Blonde Repair — Blonde-Specific Reconstruction

Built on: Protein blend (hydrolyzed), oil blend, shea butter, amino acids, panthenol.

For: Bleached, blonde, or highlighted hair.

Job: Regeneration and strength for bleached fibre. Damage repair plus mass replacement.

7 SKUs. Shampoo + Conditioner (250ml + 1L), Mask (200g + 500g), Leave-In (200g).

Defense — Scalp + Anti-Hair-Loss

For: Hair loss prevention and scalp treatment.

Job: Prevents hair loss (different from preventing breakage — Defense targets the follicle, not the fibre).

Apply to scalp, not the lengths, and don't rinse. The FAQ specifically notes Defense ampoule "must be applied to the scalp and without rinsing" — opposite protocol to all the other ampoules.

The decision matrix

Hair conditionPrimary lineLayered support
Dry, dull, intactEssential—
Dry + frizzyDivineEssential Oil Blend
Curly, dehydratedEssentialDivine for mask rotation
Colored, fadingSoul ColorEssential for hydration
Bleached, dryBond AngelEssential Repair Ampoule
Bleached, breakingBond AngelEssential Anti-Breakage Ampoule
Severely damagedRevivalBond Angel if also blonde
Hair loss / thinningDefenseEssential for the lengths
Post-chemical-cutRevival or Essential Anti-BreakageBond Angel if blonde

Common pairings the FAQ confirms

Essential + Soul Color

"The Essential line is perfect for repairing strands damaged by the coloring process and for a better result it can be interspersed with the Soul Color line, which promotes colour protection."

Essential ampoules can be used with shampoos from other Brae lines

"Yes, the ampoules can be used with shampoos and conditioners from other Brae lines, according to the specific needs of each consumer."

Essential Anti-Breakage + Bond Angel + Revival

"For porous hair, the Essential Antibreak, Bond Angel, Revival, and Divine ampoules are indicated for porous hair. It is also possible to intersperse their use, setting up a capillary schedule, in cases of greater need."

Difference between ampoules — direct quotes from the FAQ

Essential Repair vs Divine ampoule: "The Divine ampoule provides hydration and nutrition to the strands, while the Essential Repair ampoule provides hydration and reconstruction."

Essential Repair vs Revival ampoule: "The Essential Repair ampoule has hydration as its main benefit, while the Revival ampoule offers reconstruction."

Essential Anti-Breakage vs Defense ampoule: "The Essential Anti-Breakage ampoule offers the benefit of preventing hair breakage, while the Defense ampoule prevents hair loss."

Essential Anti-Breakage vs Bond Angel ampoule: "The Essential Anti-Breakage ampoule offers a fibre reconstruction treatment from the first application, helping to stabilize hair breakage while deeply moisturizing and strengthening the hair. The Bond Angel ampoule provides a reconstructive, fortifying with antioxidant properties to preserve the colour of bleached hair (especially blonde), with a lot of emollience and softness."

The "no wrong answer" cases

Some lines overlap enough that either works. The FAQ confirms:

  • Curly/frizzy hair: Essential ampoules suit all curvature types. Pick Anti-Breakage for broken curls, Repair for damaged/dry curls.
  • Thin or thick hair: All Brae ampoules suit all hair textures — fine, medium, coarse.
  • Bleached hair + Essential: "No problem, on the contrary, you can intersperse the use of Essential Repair, Essential Anti-Breakage, and Bond Angel."

The youngest user the line is suitable for

The FAQ specifies: ampoules are suitable from 12 years old, not younger.

The minimum routine for a single line

If a client is loyal to one Brae line only, the minimum effective routine is:

  1. Line's Shampoo
  2. Line's Conditioner
  3. Line's Mask (1-2x/week)
  4. Line's leave-in or oil finisher (daily)

Add an ampoule from the matching line at 1-2x/week for active conditions. That's the four-to-five-product home routine.

For salons, the strategic move is to sell across lines — Essential for daily, Revival or Bond Angel for problem zones, Defense for scalp. That's the six-to-eight-product routine and the higher retail ticket.

title: Brae Revival: Deep Reconstruction with Seaweed Extract and Wheat Protein
seo_title: Brae Revival Line — Seaweed + Protein Reconstruction Guide
seo_description: Brae Revival uses seaweed extract, butter blend, and triple protein (wheat/almond/oat) for extremely damaged hair. Full 15-SKU line guide.
excerpt: When the fibre's actually destroyed, Essential won't save it. Revival is the line built for the cases everyone else has given up on.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
Most professional brands have a "damaged hair" line. Some of them deserve the label. Brae Revival is one that does — built for chemically treated hair with porous, extremely damaged strands. The diagnosis is right there in the Brae documentation: "chemically treated hair, with porous and extremely damaged strands."

This isn't the line for dry hair. Dry hair belongs in Essential. Revival is the rescue line.

The 15 SKUs

Shampoo and Conditioner

  • Shampoo — 60g travel, 250ml retail, 1L professional
  • Conditioner — 60g travel, 250ml retail, 1L professional

Treatment

  • Mask — 15g sachet, 60g travel, 200g retail, 500g professional
  • Ampoule — 13ml

Travel kit

  • 60g sizes of Shampoo, Conditioner, and Mask — a full mini-routine in one box

Finishers

  • Leave-In — 200ml
  • Intense Shine Spray — 150ml
  • Gorgeous Shine Oil — 60ml

The active stack that makes it work

Butter blend (Shorea + Shea)

Shorea butter is the under-appreciated half. Sourced from Indian and Southeast Asian Sal trees, Shorea butter is higher in stearic acid than shea — meaning a harder consistency, longer-lasting film, and deeper sealing capacity. The blend with shea balances heaviness against pliability. The result: emollience and nutrition that doesn't wash out after the first rinse.

Seaweed extract

The technological active. The dossier describes it as "an active with a three-dimensional matrix, which forms a film responsible for sealing the ingredients and prolonging their duration on the hair, in addition to increasing the resistance and elasticity of the hair fibre."

Translation: seaweed extract creates a meshwork over the cuticle that holds the rest of the formula in place across multiple washes. The mass replacement effect is cumulative — each treatment builds on the last because the previous treatment hasn't yet washed out.

Wheat, almond, and oat protein

Three hydrolyzed proteins, three different molecular weights. The combination provides restructuring, hydration, regeneration, mass replacement, and protection. The triple-protein approach means the formula fills cortex gaps at three different size scales — large, medium, small — instead of relying on one protein and hoping it fits every defect.

Vegetable oil blend

Avocado, coconut, sunflower, argan, flaxseed, macadamia, olive. Seven-oil complex — the same blend Brae uses in the Blonde Repair shampoo and elsewhere. Intense and deep nutrition, softness, luminosity, prevents water loss.

Amino acids

Strengthen the hair structure, increase resistance and shine, improve the sensory — both wet (combability, softness) and dry (silky appearance).

Panthenol

Standard moisture binder. Long-lasting moisturizer, prevents damage to the hair.

How to use the Revival line

The shampoo + conditioner

Daily use, though many users alternate with Essential for daily and use Revival 2-3x per week.

Shampoo: apply to wet hair, massage to lather, rinse. Repeat if needed.

Conditioner: after shampoo, apply to ends, massage and slide between fingers to detangle, leave on a few minutes, rinse.

The mask

Once a week or as needed. After Revival Shampoo, apply mask strand by strand to damp hair, starting at ends. Gently massage to lengths. Leave on 10 minutes. Rinse thoroughly.

Pro tip from the manual: use a few drops of Revival Gorgeous Shine Oil along with the mask to enhance hydration and shine. The mask + oil combo is the standard salon-grade move for the heaviest damage.

The ampoule

1-2 times a week as needed. Wash with Revival shampoo. Remove excess moisture. Divide hair into 4 sections. Distribute about 4ml of the ampoule between the sections. Massage and leave on 3 minutes. Rinse thoroughly. No conditioner required after.

Pro tip from the manual: mix the ampoule with the Revival Mask using a spatula to create an even more potent and personalised treatment.

Travel kit — the underrated SKU

The 60g travel size box includes Shampoo, Conditioner, and Mask. A full mini-routine in one purchase. Useful for:

  • Trial purchases before committing to full sizes
  • Travel obviously, but also
  • Cross-line clients who use another line as their daily and Revival as their rescue intervention
  • Gifts and salon retail "try this" upsell tools

Who Revival is for

The dossier diagnosis: "chemically treated hair, with porous and extremely damaged strands."

In practice: post-bleach disasters, multi-step colour services, smoothing-and-bleach combinations, fibre that's lost elasticity, heat-styling damage that's been progressing for months without intervention, or any client who comes in saying "everything is broken."

How it compares to Essential

The FAQ from the Essential section addresses this directly. Essential Repair ampoule has hydration as its main benefit. Revival ampoule offers reconstruction. Two different problems, two different lines.

For a client who's both dehydrated AND broken — most clients with bleach in their history — the answer is both lines, alternating across the capillary schedule. Essential for hydration days, Revival for reconstruction days.

Why hyaluronic acid for hair

Hyaluronic acid is a polysaccharide that binds up to 1,000 times its weight in water. In skin care, it's the molecule that gives plump, hydrated skin. In hair, the same property delivers prolonged hydration without weighing fibre down.

The dossier emphasizes its specific actions in hair: high hydration power, strengthening of the strands, protection of the hair fibre, and repair of split ends. This isn't a marketing position — it's the documented behaviour of hyaluronic acid at the fibre level.

The supporting active stack

Hyaluronic acid alone wouldn't reconstruct. Brae pairs it with amino acids and complementary actives line-wide:

  • Protein blend (hydrolyzed) — Broken down to smaller chains for rapid absorption. Protects against external damage, adds shine, vitality, hydration, nutrition.

Who Essential is for — and who it isn't for

The Essential line is suitable for dry, dull hair across all hair types. It excels at daily hydration and moderate-damage repair.

It is not the line for severely broken or chemically destroyed fibre. Per the dossier, that's where the Essential Anti-Breakage (Antiquebra) products and the Brae Revival line take over. The Essential Repair Ampoule handles moderate damage; the Essential Anti-Breakage Ampoule handles severe damage.

title: Hyaluronic Acid in Hair Care: What It Actually Does to Fibre
seo_title: Hyaluronic Acid for Hair — How It Works Explained
seo_description: Hyaluronic acid binds 1,000x its weight in water. In hair care, it delivers prolonged hydration without buildup. Full explainer.
excerpt: Skin care discovered hyaluronic acid decades ago. Hair care is catching up. Here's why the molecule works in fibre, not just under skin.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
Hyaluronic acid spent the 2010s becoming the most-recognized active in dermatology. Every skin care brand from drugstore to luxury added it to serums, creams, and injectables. The molecule binds up to 1,000 times its weight in water, and that single property changed how skin care formulators think about hydration.

Hair care arrived at hyaluronic acid later. Brae's Essential line is one of the larger Brazilian deployments — a full 13-SKU system built around the molecule.

The molecule itself

Hyaluronic acid is a glycosaminoglycan — a long polymer chain of repeating disaccharide units (D-glucuronic acid and N-acetyl-D-glucosamine). The chain is highly hydrophilic. Each unit attracts and holds water molecules through hydrogen bonding.

The result is a molecule that behaves like a sponge — drawing in water from the environment, holding it against evaporation, releasing it slowly into the tissue it's attached to.

In skin care

Hyaluronic acid is a natural component of the dermis. As skin ages, native hyaluronic acid decreases, contributing to the loss of plumpness and elasticity. Topical and injected forms replace what the body no longer makes in sufficient quantity.

This is the use case that built the molecule's reputation. Plump-looking skin = hydrated skin = hyaluronic acid-rich skin.

In hair care — what it actually does

Hair isn't living tissue, but it isn't dead either — it's a hygroscopic structure that constantly exchanges moisture with the environment. Dehydrated fibre is brittle, dull, and unmanageable. Over-hydrated fibre is limp.

Hyaluronic acid delivers a controlled equilibrium. Per the Brae Essential dossier, its documented actions in hair:

  • High hydration power — Binds water from the formulation and from atmospheric moisture, depositing it at the cuticle and cortex level.
  • Strengthening of the strands — Hydrated fibre has higher tensile strength. Dry fibre breaks at lower stress.
  • Protection of the hair fibre — Forms a hydrophilic film that buffers against environmental humidity swings (the cause of frizz).
  • Repair of split ends — Penetrates the porous tip of damaged fibre, filling the cortical gaps that produce splits.

Why hyaluronic acid in shampoo isn't a gimmick

The common objection is "you rinse the shampoo out — why put expensive actives in it?" For most surfactant-based actives, the objection holds. For hyaluronic acid, it doesn't.

Hyaluronic acid has affinity for keratin proteins through hydrogen bonding. During the lather phase, the molecule binds to the cuticle. The rinse removes the surfactant but the hyaluronic acid stays. The result is hair that's cleaner AND more hydrated than it was before the wash.

Where it sits in a capillary schedule

The Brae FAQ places the Essential mask in the hydration stage of a capillary schedule. A typical Brazilian three-stage schedule runs:

  1. Hydration — Water and moisture replacement. Hyaluronic acid lines (Essential), aloe vera, glycerin.
  2. Nutrition — Lipid and oil replacement. Avocado oil, shea butter, argan.
  3. Reconstruction — Protein and structural replacement. Hydrolyzed keratin, amino acids, fibroin.

Essential primarily targets stage 1, with overlap into stage 2 (via the Oil Blend SKU) and stage 3 (via the amino acid blend and the Anti-Breakage Ampoule).

How to combine with other actives

Hyaluronic acid plays well with everything. It's not pH-sensitive in the cosmetic range, doesn't compete with proteins for binding sites, and doesn't get blocked by silicones.

The Brae Essential FAQ confirms you can mix the Essential Oil Blend into the mask to enhance results, mix ampoules into the mask for deeper penetration, and intersperse with Soul Color products for colored hair.

Who hyaluronic acid hair care is for

Best results on dry, dull, environmentally-stressed fibre. The molecule is hydration-focused, not reconstruction-focused. For severely broken hair, the line that combines hyaluronic acid with high-protein reconstruction (Brae's Anti-Breakage variants, or other brands' equivalent) outperforms a pure hyaluronic line.

For colored hair, the molecule helps retain moisture lost during the chemical service. For curly hair, it supports curl elasticity by maintaining cortex hydration. For straight, dehydrated fibre, it delivers the daily moisture the cuticle can't manufacture itself.

title: The Brazilian Capillary Schedule: Hydration, Nutrition, Reconstruction
seo_title: Brazilian Capillary Schedule — Cronograma Capilar Guide
seo_description: The Brazilian capillary schedule rotates hydration, nutrition, and reconstruction treatments across the week. Full method explained.
excerpt: In Brazil it's called cronograma capilar. In Europe it's still a niche secret. Here's the three-stage rotation that defines Brazilian salon-grade home care.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
The Brazilian beauty industry has a concept European hair care never developed — the cronograma capilar, or capillary schedule. It's not a product. It's a method. A weekly rotation of three treatment types that each address a specific deficiency in the fibre.

If you've ever used the same mask twice a week for a month and watched your hair get worse, the cronograma is the missing context. You weren't using the wrong product. You were using one product when the fibre needed three.

The three stages

1. Hydration

Replaces water lost from the cuticle and cortex. Counters frizz, dullness, and the rough feel of dehydrated fibre.

Hero actives: Hyaluronic acid, aloe vera, glycerin, panthenol, D-Pantenol.

Brae line: Essential.

Other Brazilian brands: Tanino Therapy Hydra Fusion (Salvatore), Honma H-Sos Capilar hydration step, most Cadiveu Nutri products.

2. Nutrition

Replaces lipids the fibre has lost through washing, sun exposure, and chemical service. Restores softness, sealing, and shine.

Hero actives: Vegetable oils (argan, macadamia, coconut, avocado, olive), shea butter, ceramides.

Brae line: Essential Oil Blend, Divine line.

Other Brazilian brands: Honma H-Hair Care line, Salvatore Resistance oil blend.

3. Reconstruction

Replaces structural proteins lost from the cortex due to chemical or mechanical damage. Restores tensile strength and elasticity.

Hero actives: Hydrolyzed keratin, amino acids (cysteine, alanine, arginine), collagen, hydrolyzed wheat protein.

Brae line: Essential Anti-Breakage Ampoule, Revival, Bond Angel.

Other Brazilian brands: Salvatore Resistance (Luna Matrix), Honma H-Bond Plex.

The rotation logic

The schedule isn't "do all three every wash." It's a rotation, calibrated to the fibre's dominant need.

Healthy fibre, no chemical service

2x hydration + 1x nutrition per week. Reconstruction monthly or skip entirely.

Colour-treated, no bleach

2x hydration + 1x nutrition + 1x reconstruction per week. Mask rotation cycles through all three.

Bleached or chemically smoothed

1x hydration + 1x nutrition + 2x reconstruction per week. Reconstruction is the dominant need — the fibre has lost protein.

Curly, dry, no chemical service

3x hydration + 1x nutrition per week. Hydration is the main deficiency.

Post-chemical-cut or actively breaking

1x hydration + 3x reconstruction per week (for two weeks), then return to balanced rotation.

Why protein overload is real

European beauty culture talks about deep conditioning as "always good." Brazilian salon culture knows that too much protein, too often, produces protein overload — fibre that's rigid, snaps under tension, and looks straw-like.

The cronograma prevents protein overload by definition. If you're rotating hydration and nutrition in alongside reconstruction, you can't accidentally protein-overload the fibre. You can if you're using only one mask type all the time.

How to set up your own schedule

Step 1: Diagnose the fibre

Strand test. Take a clean dry strand. Stretch it gently.

  • If it snaps quickly with little stretch → low elasticity, needs HYDRATION.
  • If it stretches and stays stretched → high elasticity, needs NUTRITION + RECONSTRUCTION (it's over-hydrated).
  • If it stretches and snaps in the middle → balanced but damaged, needs RECONSTRUCTION primarily.
  • If it stretches and bounces back → balanced. Maintain.

Step 2: Pick a line for each stage

Brae makes this clean — Essential for hydration, Divine for nutrition, Revival or Bond Angel for reconstruction. Other brands have their own three-line architectures.

Step 3: Schedule the week

Wash 1: hydration mask. Wash 2: nutrition mask. Wash 3: reconstruction mask. Repeat. Track for two weeks. Re-test strand at the end.

Step 4: Adjust

If the fibre still feels rigid, dial back reconstruction. If it still feels limp, dial back hydration. The schedule isn't fixed — it's responsive.

The professional version

Salons offer the cronograma as a service — three different treatments across three different visits over a month. Each visit uses the appropriate professional-strength mask plus ampoule for that stage. Between visits, the client maintains with retail-strength versions of the same line.

This is the commercial structure that turns a one-off treatment into a four-visit subscription. Salons running the cronograma as a service see significantly higher per-client revenue than salons that sell single treatments.

title: Mix Therapy Exclusive: How Salvatore's Custom Protocol System Works
seo_title: Salvatore Mix Therapy — Custom Protocol Recipe Guide
seo_description: Mix Therapy from Salvatore Tanino Therapy Exclusive — the recipe book for combining lines. Custom protocols for every fibre condition.
excerpt: No two heads of hair are identical. Mix Therapy is Salvatore's recipe library — cross-line combinations engineered for every fibre problem you'll meet behind the chair.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
The pretty package on the shelf is the marketing layer. The real value of Tanino Therapy Exclusive is what happens when you ignore the line boundaries and start mixing.

The dossier ships with a section called Mix Therapy — a recipe book of cross-line combinations. Each recipe is a named protocol with specific products, specific dosages, and a specific fibre condition it targets. This is where Salvatore's seven-line architecture stops being a catalog and starts being a chemistry library.

The categories of recipes

Mix Therapy organizes recipes into seven categories:

  • Alinhamento e Reestruturação — smoothing and structural realignment
  • Reconstrução — reconstruction
  • Nutrição de Loiros — blonde nutrition
  • Hidratação Intensiva — intensive hydration
  • Nutrição de Cachos — curl nutrition
  • Finalização — finishing
  • Blond Repair System — bleach reinforcement

A few named recipes worth knowing

Alinhamento Capilar Taninoplastia

40ml of A + 60ml of B. The base TANINOPLASTIA® protocol — Cuticle Prepper followed by Capillary Styling. Smoothing service for most fibre types.

Resset

10–20ml A + B + 30ml Revitalize Chemical mask + 20g Hydra Fusion mask + 5–10g Nutri Curl leave-in (as needed). A reconstruction reset for fibre that's been through too many services. This is the recipe for a client who comes in saying "I don't know what's wrong, but everything we try fails." Combines five products from four different lines.

Force Repair

5g Resistance mask + 5g Hydra Fusion mask + 5g Resistance leave-in + 5g Radiant Color mask + 1 pump Hydra Fusion oil. For severe damage with colour retention need.

Stop Breakage Solution

5g Revitalize Chemical mask + 15ml Hydra Fusion shampoo + B + 5g Resistance mask. For active breakage that won't stop with hydration alone — needs metal removal first, then reconstruction.

Curly Definition

10–15ml Nutri Curl shampoo + 15ml B + 10g Revitalize Chemical mask + 10g Nutri Curl mask + Nutri Curl leave-in as needed. The full curl reset for clients who haven't had real curl care.

Nano Matiz / Soft Platinum

Multiple blonde nutrition combos. Nano Matiz uses Hydra Fusion or Nutri Curl shampoo (20ml) + Resistance mask (5g) + Vitality Blond mask (5g). Soft Platinum uses Hydra Fusion or Nutri Curl shampoo (10–15ml) + Revitalize Chemical mask (5g) + Vitality Blond mask (5g). Both designed to tone while nourishing — most violet shampoos and masks dry the hair, these don't.

What the recipes signal about the brand

Brands that ship a recipe book are brands that expect their professionals to think. Mix Therapy isn't telling you "use product X for problem Y." It's telling you "here's the chemistry library, here are 20 worked examples, now build your own."

This is the difference between a brand and a system. Brands sell SKUs. Systems sell chemistry literacy. Salvatore is selling chemistry literacy.

How to actually use Mix Therapy in a salon

1. Diagnose first

Mix Therapy assumes you've done a real consultation — porosity, elasticity, metal load, colour history, breakage pattern. The recipes target specific conditions, not generic "dry hair."

2. Identify primary and secondary needs

Most clients have one dominant issue (e.g., damage) and one secondary issue (e.g., colour fade). The recipes are built to address combined conditions. Pure single-need treatments are usually one line alone.

3. Don't improvise without understanding pH

The line-by-line pH map matters. Shampoos run 4.5–5.5 (slightly alkaline for cleaning). Masks and conditioners run 3.5–4.5 (acidic for cuticle close). Leave-ins and serums run 3.5–4.5. If you mix outside these ranges, you're working against the chemistry.

4. Use the dossier's exact dosages

The dosages are tested. "A little of this, a lot of that" doesn't produce the same result.

The recipes are also a marketing tool

A salon that names its services by Mix Therapy recipe (e.g., "Resset Reconstruction" instead of "deep treatment") signals expertise to the client. The recipe names are technical enough to feel premium and specific enough to differentiate the service from a generic mask treatment.

title: Salvatore Blond Repair System: TT Plex Technology for Bleached Hair
seo_title: Salvatore Blond Repair System — TT Plex Bleach Protection
seo_description: Total Injection Repair + Serum Reconstructor + Fibre Force from Salvatore. TT Plex technology reinforces disulfide bonds during bleaching.
excerpt: Three products that protect the disulfide bond during bleach, replace lost mass during recovery, and seal the result. Built around TT Plex technology.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
Bleach breaks disulfide bonds. Every professional knows this. Most also know that products like Olaplex, K18, and others have built billion-dollar businesses around protecting those bonds. What's less commonly known is that Salvatore has its own bond-protection system — TT Plex — built natively into the Tanino Therapy Exclusive platform.

The Blond Repair System is three products: Total Injection Repair, Sérum Reconstructor, and Fibre Force. Together they cover pre-treatment, in-process protection, and recovery.

The three products

Total Injection Repair

pH 3.5 to 4.5, 300ml. The hero product. Recovers and strengthens fibre damaged by chemical processes. Replaces keratin and fills internal cortex layers, preventing future ruptures. Reconstruction system and capillary mass replacement.

Sérum Reconstructor

pH 4.0 to 5.0, 300ml. The recovery and protection arm. Restores moisture after lifting, complements the mass replacement, repairs split ends, gives high thermal protection for mechanical and heat finishing.

Fibre Force

pH 3.5, 300ml. High-penetration mass replacement. Deep hydration, sedosidade, colour protection. Used during and after chemical services.

How TT Plex actually works

The dossier illustrates the mechanism with a three-panel diagram of the disulfide bond:

  • Panel A — Natural hair, chemical-free. Disulfide bonds intact between cystine residues.
  • Panel B — Disulfide bond being broken by the bleach action. Persulfate ions cleave the S-S bond.
  • Panel C — Disulfide bond being broken by bleach action AND simultaneously re-established by Total Injection Repair.

The mechanism: persulfates in the bleach formula remove melanin AND cleave disulfide bridges. Without intervention, those bridges stay broken. Total Injection Repair, mixed into the bleach mixture itself, contributes amino acids (cysteine, glycine, glutamine, alanine) and structural materials that re-form bridges in real time.

The actives stack

  • Tanino — conducts the actives into the fibre, increases adherence, restores resistance and density.
  • Luna Matrix — the same Salvatore-registered amino acid blend used in the Resistance line, creating a unique restructuring system that fills cortex fissures.
  • Collagen — internal repair, flexibility, force, with high affinity for keratin.
  • D-Panthenol — restores moisture.
  • Amino acids and proteins — cystine, glycine, glutamine, alanine — promote resistance.

Application — mixed into the bleach

Unlike a separate pre-treatment or post-treatment, Total Injection Repair is designed to go INTO the bleach mixture. This is the "TTPLEX" claim — protection happens during the chemical reaction, not before or after. The fibre gets bleached and re-bonded simultaneously.

The benefits the dossier names:

  • Protection of fibers during chemical processes
  • Repair of extremely damaged fibers
  • Force and resistance guarantee
  • Longer-lasting colour results
  • Soft touch and UV protection

Compatibility with other Salvatore services

The Blond Repair System is compatible with every other chemical service in the Salvatore portfolio — Tanino Colors permanent coloring, Creare tonalizante, Fast Effect bleach powder, and the TANINOPLASTIA® smoothing protocol. Because the underlying chemistry shares the same Tanino base, there's no incompatibility to manage.

Pricing strategy implication for salons

Bleach services are the most profitable and most risky in the salon menu. The risk drives clients away. Adding Blond Repair System to every bleach service — and charging for the upgrade — converts the risk into a tier-up. The same client who would have refused a bleach service because of breakage history says yes when you offer the "with TT Plex protection" version.

The math is also direct. Total Injection Repair adds material cost per service, but the upcharge typically runs 30–50% over the base bleach price, and the success rate climbs.

title: Tanino Colors: The First Colour Line Built on the Tanino Active
seo_title: Tanino Colors — Salvatore's Permanent Hair Colour Guide
seo_description: Tanino Colors from Salvatore — 60 permanent tones, TANINNteract technology, Ceril-Protect® film. First colour line with Tanino active base.
excerpt: Sixty tones, an ammonia-light formula, and a Tanino base nobody else has. Here's why Salvatore's colour line plays differently than the European majors.
author: Tomás Costa
content:
The professional hair colour market is dominated by a handful of European houses — Wella, L'Oréal, Schwarzkopf, Goldwell. Their formulas all share the same architectural assumption: ammonia opens the cuticle, peroxide oxidizes the natural melanin, intermediate dyes couple inside the cortex.

Tanino Colors changes the base. It's the first permanent colour line built on Tanino — Salvatore's polyphenol active — as part of the colour base itself.

The basics

TANINNteract — what it does

Ceril-Protect® — the second technology

The formula is enriched with Ceril-Protect®. This is a film-forming technology that aligns the cuticle during colour application, preserving the fibre from loss of pigment molecules and hydration. The film does three things:

  1. Aligns cuticle scales for even dye deposit.
  2. Prevents pigment escape during the processing time.

The colour chart — what's worth noting

The Ox Tanino is itself a Salvatore product — emulsion with encapsulated intelligent technology that activates after reaching a certain oxidation level, balancing the process and controlling damage.

Unified chemistry. The post-color care (Radiant Color) is engineered for the colors. The bond reinforcement (TT Plex Blond Repair System) is engineered for the bleach. The pre-chemistry detox (Revitalize Chemical) is engineered for the metals. Every element of the chain shares the Tanino base.

title: Colore Gel: Salvatore's Gel-Based Colour Deposit System Explained
seo_title: Salvatore Colore Gel — Gel Colour Deposit System Guide
seo_description: Colore Gel from Salvatore — first gel-based permanent colour. Micellar penetration, bioadherent shield, 20-minute action. Full technology guide.
excerpt: Cream-base colors have ruled the salon for decades. Salvatore's Colore Gel changes the base — micellar penetration in nano-spheres, then a bioadherent shield seals the result.
author: Camila Ferreira
content:
For decades, the professional colour industry depended on cream bases. Although functional, cream bases bring chemical and mechanical limitations: they contain many emulsifiers that delay pigment oxidation and complicate application.

Colore Gel breaks the paradigm. Salvatore developed a translucent polymeric gel base that doesn't just transport colour — it optimizes every step of the chemical and physical process inside the fibre.

The four pillars

Pillar 1 — Micelle science

The secret of Colore Gel performance isn't only what it contains — it's how it organizes microscopically when mixed. Unlike cream, which arrives pre-emulsified, the gel base activates at the moment of hydration (mixing with the developer). At that moment, structures called Micelles form. Think of them as intelligent nano-spheres.

These micelles work as transport vehicles. Being extremely reduced and fluid, they navigate through cuticles with minimal resistance, carrying pigments and treatment actives directly to the cortex.

Pillar 2 — Gel rheology

Three direct effects of the gel structure:

  • Free oxidation, fast action — As the gel base is neutral and translucent, it doesn't contain the chemical impediments of cream bases. Pigment precursors reveal directly and immediately on contact with the cortex.
  • Glide and conditioning — Application is a different tactile experience. The brush slides without friction, detangling hair instantly. High-conditioning base treats the fibre during coloring.
  • Profitability — Due to high spreadability and fluidity, Colore Gel covers a much larger surface area than the same quantity of cream colour. Less product per client, higher profitability per service.

Pillar 3 — Bioadherent shield

Bioaderência refers to the product's capacity to biologically fix to the proteins of the capillary fibre. After the pigments deposit in the cortex through the micelles, the gel base stabilizes and creates an invisible, resistant protective film over the cuticle.

This barrier seals the pigments inside the fibre, preventing them from being "pulled out" easily during daily washing. The result is a vibrant colour for much longer and a three-dimensional shine.

Pillar 4 — Colour Gel Deposit System Technology

Anti-fade shield technology. The complete package: micelles as the vehicle, bioadherence as the shield.

The user benefits

  • Speed — Accelerated penetration by nano micelles. 20-minute action time.
  • Precision — Oxidation without interference for faithful colors.
  • Profitability — High glide and superior yield.
  • Durability — Bioadherent anti-fade shielding.

The package

Colore Gel ships as 60g tubes. Used with Ox Colore Gel oxidant (20 vol., 6%) in a 1:1 ratio. The combination is 100% ammonia-free, 100% gray coverage, 20-minute action.

Why this matters competitively

Gel-based colour is rare. A few European brands have experimented with gel bases but most retreated to cream because the formulation is harder. Salvatore's investment in the micelle + bioaderência system is a generational technology bet — and the results in the dossier (cleaner application, faster processing, longer colour life) suggest the bet is paying off.

For salons considering Tanino Colors, the choice between cream (standard Tanino Colors) and Colore Gel comes down to client positioning. Cream is familiar. Gel is premium, faster, and produces a more vibrant result — and it justifies a premium price point.
